title: Global, Regional, and National Cancer Incidence, Mortality, Years of Life Lost, Years Lived With Disability, and Disability-Adjusted Life-Years for 29 Cancer Groups, 1990 to 2017: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study
human: Cancer and other noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) are now widely recognized as a threat to global development. The latest United Nations high-level meeting on NCDs reaffirmed this observation and also highlighted the slow progress in meeting the 2011 Political Declaration on the Prevention and Control of Noncommunicable Diseases and the third Sustainable Development Goal. Lack of situational analyses, priority setting, and budgeting have been identified as major obstacles in achieving these goals. All of these have in common that they require information on the local cancer epidemiology. The Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study is uniquely poised to provide these crucial data. To describe cancer burden for 29 cancer groups in 195 countries from 1990 through 2017 to provide data needed for cancer control planning. We used the GBD study estimation methods to describe cancer incidence, mortality, years lived with disability, years of life lost, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs). Results are presented at the national level as well as by Socio-demographic Index (SDI), a composite indicator of income, educational attainment, and total fertility rate. We also analyzed the influence of the epidemiological vs the demographic transition on cancer incidence. In 2017, there were 24.5 million incident cancer cases worldwide (16.8 million without nonmelanoma skin cancer [NMSC]) and 9.6 million cancer deaths. The majority of cancer DALYs came from years of life lost (97%), and only 3% came from years lived with disability. The odds of developing cancer were the lowest in the low SDI quintile (1 in 7) and the highest in the high SDI quintile (1 in 2) for both sexes. In 2017, the most common incident cancers in men were NMSC (4.3 million incident cases); tracheal, bronchus, and lung (TBL) cancer (1.5 million incident cases); and prostate cancer (1.3 million incident cases). The most common causes of cancer deaths and DALYs for men were TBL cancer (1.3 million deaths and 28.4 million DALYs), liver cancer (572 000 deaths and 15.2 million DALYs), and stomach cancer (542 000 deaths and 12.2 million DALYs). For women in 2017, the most common incident cancers were NMSC (3.3 million incident cases), breast cancer (1.9 million incident cases), and colorectal cancer (819 000 incident cases). The leading causes of cancer deaths and DALYs for women were breast cancer (601 000 deaths and 17.4 million DALYs), TBL cancer (596 000 deaths and 12.6 million DALYs), and colorectal cancer (414 000 deaths and 8.3 million DALYs). The national epidemiological profiles of cancer burden in the GBD study show large heterogeneities, which are a reflection of different exposures to risk factors, economic settings, lifestyles, and access to care and screening. The GBD study can be used by policy makers and other stakeholders to develop and improve national and local cancer control in order to achieve the global targets and improve equity in cancer care.

title: classic-329
human:
In a row on the shelf stood the loaves and, beside them, on a big white dish lay the pasties. Sabina had added onion and bacon to make them appetizing, parsley to give flavour, freshly dug potatoes to hold the gravy; and all was folded in a responsible crust. Her pasties were renowned; but Byron, satisfying his hunger, did not notice the quality of the food. He was still obsessed by his vision of the empty house. The barren years, when he had paced the friendly fields as a captive paces his cage, unable either to take action or to escape, had done their work. He had supported life on a meagre hope; but he was older now, less patient, had a shorter time left him in which to enjoy. The young Samson can afford to ask riddles and play tricks, it is the ageing man who, grown desperate, brings destruction upon the people. Standing by the shelf, eating hungrily but absent-mindedly, Byron presently became conscious of voices in the kitchen. For a moment his heart beat in swift anticipation. Was Gray back? He stopped eating to listen, but the voice which had suggested that of the young girl was older and had lost some of its West-country music. He recognized it disappointedly as that of the girl's mother.

Filling himself a mug from the pitcher of milk that stood on the flags, Byron drank. If Mrs. Tom were in the kitchen the little party must have returned from Stowe, and the thought was, in a way, reassuring. Gray would be at Hember now and Rosevear would have come on to Wastralls with the mare and cart. At least they were no longer together.

Byron's thoughts dwelt fleetingly on Rosevear. Should he go back, find the fellow and send him packing? He hated the sight of that womanishly smooth face. Some day he would send his fist crashing into it, put the weight of his shoulder into the blow. If he could fell a bullock it would be child's play to spoil Rosevear's beauty, to make him so as the chap's own mother wouldn't recognize him. When Gray saw what he made of her fine sweetheart, there would be no more hesitation--Leadville could not believe it to be more than hesitation. She would turn to the man who had proved in primal fashion his right to her.

In the kitchen the women's voices rose and fell, lifting at the end in the Cornish way. Phrases and half words reached the man's ears and brought him to a distrustful consideration of them. These women, with their 'under-hauling,' their scheming, the way they 'held for each other'--what were they discussing? Him and his affairs? He fell to again on the pasty, biting into its hard crust with unnecessary force, biting indeed into more than crust and meat.

Mrs. Tom, having brought in the Christmas groceries and stacked the tins and parcels on the side-table, had settled down for a chat. The bond between the women, which like themselves was stout and workaday, had been embroidered by the years with a pattern of memories; and what can be pleasanter at the end of a winter day than to sit by a bright fire with a friend who has been tried by time? Sabina talked of her husband, of the farm, of the future.

Sabina stirred her tea in a meditative fashion. With a simple faith in good and evil, reward and punishment, it was puzzling to her that she who was a 'member and had gone to prayer meeting and chapel all right and been a good livin' woman,' should have had so much trouble. "I think it's a awful thing for 'e to be running after Gray, when 'e got a wife of's own?" she said. "Too bad, I do call it."

The more clear-sighted woman did not dispute the matter. Even if Sabina wanted Gray and Jim to live at Wastralls, the decision would not rest with her. Gray would not care so long as she was with Jim, but he, though good-natured and easygoing, knew his own mind. Not long since, he had been over to Gentle Jane where his aunt, receiving him warmly, had been urgent that he should live with her. He had not given a definite answer, but Mrs. Tom knew he was considering the matter.

The wife's happy-go-lucky

The barren years—when he’d paced the familiar fields like a captive in a cage, unable to act or escape—had taken their toll. He’d sustained himself on slender hope alone; but now he was older, less patient, with less time left to enjoy life. The young Samson may afford riddles and games; it is the ageing man, grown desperate, who brings ruin upon others. Standing by the shelf, eating hungrily yet absently, Byron suddenly became aware of voices in the kitchen. His heart leapt—was Gray back? He paused mid-bite to listen, but the voice that had briefly echoed the girl’s was older, its West Country lilt softened by time. Disappointed, he recognized it as the mother’s.

He poured himself a mug of milk from the pitcher resting on the flagstones and drank. If Mrs. Tom was in the kitchen, the little party must have returned from Stowe—and that, in a way, was reassuring. Gray would now be at Hember; Rosevear, meanwhile, would have driven the mare and cart on to Wastralls. At least they were no longer together.

Byron’s thoughts flickered briefly to Rosevear. Should he go back, track the man down, and send him away? He loathed that smooth, almost womanish face. One day, he’d drive his fist into it—put his full shoulder behind the blow. If he could fell a bullock, unmaking Rosevear’s looks would be child’s play—leaving him so disfigured even his own mother wouldn’t know him. When Gray saw what he’d done to her fine sweetheart, there’d be no more hesitation—Leadville could only interpret it as hesitation. She’d turn, then, to the man who’d claimed her—not with words, but with primal, undeniable proof.

In the kitchen, the women’s voices rose and fell, lifting at the ends in the Cornish manner. Fragments of phrases and half-heard words drifted to him, stirring suspicion. These women—with their “under-hauling,” their quiet scheming, the way they “held for each other”—what were they discussing? Him? His affairs? He resumed eating, biting into the pasty’s hard crust with unnecessary force—biting, it seemed, into something far deeper than pastry and meat.

The bond between the women—like themselves—was solid and practical, its texture enriched over the years with shared memories. title: A machine learning-based framework for modeling transcription elongation
human: RNA polymerase II (Pol II) generally pauses at certain positions along gene bodies, thereby interrupting the transcription elongation process, which is often coupled with various important biological functions, such as precursor mRNA splicing and gene expression regulation. Characterizing the transcriptional elongation dynamics can thus help us understand many essential biological processes in eukaryotic cells. However, experimentally measuring Pol II elongation rates is generally time and resource consuming. We developed PEPMAN (polymerase II elongation pausing modeling through attention-based deep neural network), a deep learning-based model that accurately predicts Pol II pausing sites based on the native elongating transcript sequencing (NET-seq) data. Through fully taking advantage of the attention mechanism, PEPMAN is able to decipher important sequence features underlying Pol II pausing. More importantly, we demonstrated that the analyses of the PEPMAN-predicted results around various types of alternative splicing sites can provide useful clues into understanding the cotranscriptional splicing events. In addition, associating the PEPMAN prediction results with different epigenetic features can help reveal important factors related to the transcription elongation process. All these results demonstrated that PEPMAN can provide a useful and effective tool for modeling transcription elongation and understanding the related biological factors from available high-throughput sequencing data.
text: RNA polymerase II (Pol II) frequently pauses at specific positions within gene bodies, thereby modulating transcription elongation—a process tightly coupled with critical biological functions, including precursor mRNA splicing and the regulation of gene expression. Characterizing the dynamics of transcriptional elongation is therefore essential for understanding fundamental regulatory mechanisms in eukaryotic cells. However, experimental measurement of Pol II elongation rates remains technically challenging, time-intensive, and resource-demanding. To address this limitation, we developed PEPMAN (Polymerase II Elongation Pausing Modeling through Attention-based Neural Networks), a deep learning model that accurately predicts Pol II pausing sites directly from native elongating transcript sequencing (NET-seq) data. Leveraging the attention mechanism, PEPMAN effectively identifies and prioritizes biologically relevant sequence features associated with pausing. Importantly, our analyses of PEPMAN-predicted pausing patterns around diverse alternative splicing sites yield mechanistic insights into cotranscriptional splicing. Furthermore, integrating PEPMAN predictions with epigenetic annotations reveals key regulatory factors influencing transcription elongation. Collectively, these findings establish PEPMAN as a powerful, scalable, and interpretable tool for modeling transcription elongation dynamics and uncovering associated biological determinants from high-throughput sequencing data.

title: The Effect of Manufacturing Agglomeration on Haze Pollution in China
human: Based on panel data on 285 Chinese cities from 2003 to 2012, we use a dynamic spatial panel model to empirically analyze the effect of manufacturing agglomeration on haze pollution. The results show that when economic development levels, population, technological levels, industrial structure, transportation, foreign direct investment, and greening levels are stable, manufacturing agglomeration significantly aggravates haze pollution. However, region-specific analysis reveals that the effects of manufacturing agglomeration on inter-regional haze pollution depends on the region: the effect of manufacturing agglomeration on haze pollution is the largest in the Western region, followed by the Central region, and is the least in the Eastern region. Based on the above conclusions, we put forward several specific suggestions, such as giving full play to the technology and knowledge spillover effects of manufacturing agglomeration, guiding manufacturing agglomerations in a scientific and rational way, accelerating the transformation and upgrading of manufacturing industries in agglomeration regions.
text: Using panel data from 285 Chinese cities spanning 2003–2012, we employ a dynamic spatial panel model to empirically examine the impact of manufacturing agglomeration on haze pollution. Our findings indicate that—holding constant economic development, population size, technological capability, industrial structure, transportation infrastructure, foreign direct investment, and urban greening levels—manufacturing agglomeration significantly exacerbates haze pollution. However, region-specific analyses reveal substantial heterogeneity: the adverse effect of manufacturing agglomeration on haze pollution is strongest in the Western region, intermediate in the Central region, and weakest in the Eastern region. Drawing on these results, we propose several targeted policy recommendations: (1) harnessing the technology and knowledge spillover benefits inherent in manufacturing agglomerations; (2) guiding the formation and evolution of such agglomerations through science-based, rational planning; and (3) accelerating the transformation and upgrading of manufacturing industries within agglomeration zones.

title: Organization model, vertical integration, and farmers' income growth: Empirical evidence from large-scale farmers in Lin'an, China
human: Since China's reform and opening-up in 1978, the income of rural residents has increased when compared with that of urban residents. However, the income growth rate of farmers is relatively low, and the income gap between urban and rural areas is widening. Using a sample of 1,325 large-scale farming households in Lin'an, this study constructs a theoretical path for how the level of vertical integration and an organization model affect farmers' income levels and empirically tests the path using a mediation effect analysis model. The results indicate that organization models and vertical integration are important factors that affect farmers' income levels. The total income and agricultural operation income of farmers who participate in agricultural operation organizations are greater than that of farmers who do not participate in an operation organization. In addition, the total income and agricultural operation income of farmers who produce and process and those who produce, process, and sell are higher than those of farmers who only produce. A farmers' organization model has both a direct and an indirect positive influence on their income level, with the indirect positive influence coming through the mediating variable of vertical integration. The application of the organizational model can promote the growth of rural households' total family income and agricultural income by 13.48% and 14.48% respectively, consisting of direct increases of 9.67% and 10.19%, and indirect increases of 3.81% and 4.29% through vertical integration. The results also show that access to credit, agricultural technology training, and the farmer's education level have significant positive impacts on farming income levels. The findings suggest ways to increase farmers' income by perfecting agricultural management organization systems, promoting agricultural industrialization, strengthening rural financial support, improving agricultural technical training for farmers, and increasing their level of education.

title: Full genome sequence of Brevibacillus laterosporus strain B9, a biological control strain isolated from Zhejiang, China
human: Brevibacillus laterosporus was newly classified from Bacillus laterosporus, which has ability to be used as a biological control agent in crop field. B. laterosporus strain B9 is an aerobic, motile, Gram-positive, spore-forming rod that was isolated from a field of Oryza sativa in Zhejiang, China in 2011. This bacterium has been confirmed to be a strong antagonist against bacterial brown strip of rice caused by Acidovorex avenae subsp. avenae. Here we describe the features of B. laterosporus strain B9, together with the complete genome sequence and its annotation. The 5,272,435bp genome contains 4804 protein-coding genes and 227 RNA-only encoding genes with 2 plasmids.
text: *Brevibacillus laterosporus* was recently reclassified from *Bacillus laterosporus* and shows promise as a biological control agent in agriculture. Strain B9 of *B. laterosporus* is an aerobic, motile, Gram-positive, spore-forming rod isolated in 2011 from a rice (*Oryza sativa*) field in Zhejiang, China. It has been experimentally confirmed to strongly inhibit bacterial brown stripe of rice, caused by *Acidovorax avenae* subsp. *avenae*. Here, we present the phenotypic characteristics of strain B9 along with its complete genome sequence and functional annotation. The 5,272,435-bp genome harbors 4,804 protein-coding genes and 227 RNA-only genes, and includes two plasmids.

title: Time-frequency relationship between R&D intensity, globalization, and carbon emissions in G7 countries: evidence from wavelet coherence analysis
human: The seven leading industrial countries, called the G7, are becoming a pivotal group to fulfil their emissions-reduction commitments to manage the climate crisis. This paper investigates the relationships between R&D intensity, globalization, and carbon emissions in the context of the G7 countries for the period from 1970 to 2017. Our analysis, which examines these relationships, focuses on the wavelet coherence approach to conduct time-frequency domain analyses. The empirical results show that there is heterogeneity across different time scales and frequencies for R&D intensity, globalization, and carbon emissions within each country. Specifically, R&D intensity and globalization are negatively correlated with carbon emissions for the G7 countries, except Japan, for which they are positive. The long-term correlations between R&D intensity, globalization, and carbon emissions are higher than those in the short- and medium-term periods. In addition, the multiscale connectedness network results reveal that the strongest bidirectional correlations exist between energy consumption, economic growth, and carbon emissions. Our results provide a useful reference for policymakers in the G7 countries to effectively regulate carbon emissions.
text: The Group of Seven (G7)—comprising the world’s seven largest advanced economies—plays an increasingly pivotal role in advancing global climate action through the fulfillment of its emissions-reduction commitments. This study examines the dynamic relationships among R&D intensity, globalization, and carbon emissions across the G7 countries over the period 1970–2017. Employing a wavelet coherence approach, we conduct time-frequency domain analyses to capture how these relationships evolve across different temporal scales. Our findings reveal significant heterogeneity in the associations among the variables—not only across countries but also across time scales and frequencies. Notably, R&D intensity and globalization exhibit a generally negative association with carbon emissions across the G7, with Japan representing a notable exception where both variables show a positive relationship with emissions. Moreover, long-term correlations between R&D intensity, globalization, and carbon emissions are consistently stronger than those observed in the short- and medium-term horizons. Complementing this, multiscale connectedness network analysis identifies energy consumption, economic growth, and carbon emissions as the trio exhibiting the strongest bidirectional linkages. Collectively, these insights offer empirically grounded guidance for G7 policymakers seeking effective, scale-aware strategies to regulate carbon emissions and advance climate mitigation efforts.

title: Childhood maltreatment and self-harm in Chinese adolescents: moderation and mediation via resilience
human: Published studies examining the association between childhood maltreatment (CM) and self-harm (SH) among adolescents have been accumulated. It is possible that resilience serves as a moderator or mediator in CM-SH association, nevertheless, this topic has never been thoroughly investigated. In this population-based cross-sectional study, we surveyed 3146 students aged 10-17 in southwest China. The Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), the Modified version of Adolescents Self-Harm Scale (MASHS), and the Resilience Scale for Chinese Adolescents (RSCA) were used to measure CM, SH, and resilience. Correlational analyses, hierarchical multivariate linear regression, and structural equation modeling (SEM) were performed to test the moderation and mediation of resilience in CM-SH association. Findings revealed that, resilience with its five dimensions, CM, and SH were significantly correlated with each other. Resilience partially moderated and mediated the association between CM and SH. Besides, among all dimensions of resilience, emotion regulation, interpersonal assistance, and family support presented the strongest mediation in CM-SH association. Our results highlight the importance of resilience in CM related SH among Chinese teenagers. Resilience-oriented intervention could be considered in SH intervention measures for adolescents who had experienced CM.
text: A growing body of literature has examined the association between childhood maltreatment (CM) and adolescent self-harm (SH). Although resilience is theorized to play a moderating or mediating role in this relationship, empirical evidence remains limited and inconclusive. In this population-based cross-sectional study, we surveyed 3,146 students aged 10–17 years in Southwest China. Exposure to CM was assessed using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), SH behaviors were measured with the Modified Adolescent Self-Harm Scale (MASHS), and resilience was evaluated using the Resilience Scale for Chinese Adolescents (RSCA). We employed correlational analyses, hierarchical multivariate linear regression, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to rigorously test both the moderating and mediating roles of resilience in the CM–SH association. Results indicated significant intercorrelations among CM, SH, and all five dimensions of resilience. Resilience both partially moderated and partially mediated the association between CM and SH. Among its subscales, emotion regulation, interpersonal assistance, and family support emerged as the strongest mediators in this pathway. These findings underscore the critical protective role of resilience in mitigating CM-related SH risk among Chinese adolescents. Integrating resilience-focused components into prevention and intervention programs may therefore be a promising strategy for supporting adolescents with histories of childhood maltreatment.

title: The burden of ambient air pollution on years of life lost in Wuxi, China, 2012-2015: A time-series study using a distributed lag non-linear model
human: Ambient air pollution ranks high among the risk factors that increase the global burden of disease. Previous studies focused on assessing mortality risk and were sparsely performed in populous developing countries with deteriorating environments. We conducted a time-series study to evaluate the air pollution-associated years of life lost (YLL) and mortality risk and to identify potential modifiers relating to the season and demographic characteristics. Using linear (for YLL) and Poisson (for mortality) regression models and controlling for time-varying factors, we found that an interquartile range (IQR) increase in a three-day average cumulative (lag 0-2 day) concentrations of PM2.5, PM10, NO2 and SO2 corresponded to increases in YLL of 12.09 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.98-21.20), 13.69 (95% CI: 3.32-24.07), 26.95 (95% CI: 13.99-39.91) and 24.39 (95% CI: 8.62-40.15) years, respectively, and to percent increases in mortality of 1.34% (95% CI: 0.67-2.01%), 1.56% (95% CI: 0.80-2.33%), 3.36% (95% CI: 2.39-4.33%) and 2.39% (95% CI: 1.24-3.55%), respectively. Among the specific causes of death, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases were positively associated with gaseous pollutants (NO2 and SO2), and diabetes was positively correlated with NO2 (in terms of the mortality risk). The effects of air pollutants were more pronounced in the cool season than in the warm season. The elderly (>65 years) and females were more vulnerable to air pollution. Studying effect estimates and their modifications by using YLL to detect premature death should support implementing health risk assessments, identifying susceptible groups and guiding policy-making and resource allocation according to specific local conditions.

title: Presentation of automated procedural guidance in surgical simulation: results of two randomised controlled trials
human: To investigate the effectiveness and usability of automated procedural guidance during virtual temporal bone surgery. Two randomised controlled trials were performed to evaluate the effectiveness, for medical students, of two presentation modalities of automated real-time procedural guidance in virtual reality simulation: full and step-by-step visual presentation of drillable areas. Presentation modality effectiveness was determined through a comparison of participants' dissection quality, evaluated by a blinded otologist, using a validated assessment scale. While the provision of automated guidance on procedure improved performance (full presentation, p = 0.03; step-by-step presentation, p < 0.001), usage of the two different presentation modalities was vastly different (full presentation, 3.73 per cent; step-by-step presentation, 60.40 per cent). Automated procedural guidance in virtual temporal bone surgery is effective in improving trainee performance. Step-by-step presentation of procedural guidance was engaging, and therefore more likely to be used by the participants.
text: To evaluate the effectiveness and usability of automated procedural guidance during virtual temporal bone surgery, two randomized controlled trials were conducted with medical students. These trials compared two real-time visual presentation modalities of automated guidance in virtual reality simulation: a full-area display versus a step-by-step highlighting of drillable regions. Effectiveness was assessed by comparing participants’ dissection quality—rated by a blinded otologist using a validated scale. Both modalities significantly improved performance relative to no guidance (full presentation: *p* = 0.03; step-by-step presentation: *p* < 0.001). However, usage rates differed markedly: only 3.73% of participants actively used the full-area modality, compared with 60.40% for the step-by-step version. Thus, while automated procedural guidance enhances trainee performance in virtual temporal bone surgery, the step-by-step format proved substantially more engaging—and consequently, far more frequently adopted.

title: Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated genetic transformation of Salix matsudana Koidz. using mature seeds
human: An Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation method was developed for Salix matsudana Koidz. using mature seeds as starting material. Multiple shoots were induced directly from embryonic shoot apices of germinating seeds. Although thidiazuron, 6-benzylaminopurine and zeatin induced multiple shoot induction with high frequency, zeatin (4.5 μM) was more effective for elongation of shoots and roots. title: Discrimination of nitrogen fertilizer levels of tea plant (Camellia sinensis) based on hyperspectral imaging
human: Nitrogen (N) fertilizer plays an important role in tea plantation management, with significant impacts on the photosynthetic capacity, productivity and nutrition status of tea plants. The present study aimed to establish a method for the discrimination of N fertilizer levels using hyperspectral imaging technique. Spectral data were extracted from the region of interest, followed by the first derivative to reduce background noise. Five optimal wavelengths were selected by principal component analysis. Texture features were extracted from the images at optimal wavelengths by gray-level gradient co-occurrence matrix. Support vector machine (SVM) and extreme learning machine were used to build classification models based on spectral data, optimal wavelengths, texture features and data fusion, respectively. The SVM model using fused data gave the best performance with highest correct classification rate of 100% for prediction set. The overall results indicated that visible and near-infrared hyperspectral imaging combined with SVM were effective in discriminating N fertilizer levels of tea plants. © 2018 Society of Chemical Industry.
text: Nitrogen (N) fertilizer plays a critical role in tea plantation management, significantly influencing photosynthetic capacity, yield, and nutritional status of tea plants. This study aimed to develop a hyperspectral imaging–based method for discriminating among different N fertilizer application levels. Spectral data were extracted from regions of interest and preprocessed using first-derivative transformation to suppress background noise. Principal component analysis was employed to identify five optimal wavelengths. Texture features were then extracted from images acquired at these optimal wavelengths using the gray-level gradient co-occurrence matrix (GLGCM). Classification models were constructed using support vector machine (SVM) and extreme learning machine (ELM), respectively, based on: (i) full spectral data, (ii) the five optimal wavelengths, (iii) texture features, and (iv) fused spectral–texture data. The SVM model trained on the fused dataset achieved the highest classification accuracy—100% for the prediction set. Overall, the results demonstrate that visible–near-infrared (Vis–NIR) hyperspectral imaging, coupled with SVM, provides an effective and reliable approach for non-destructively discriminating N fertilizer levels in tea plants. © 2018 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Whole genome sequence of Auricularia heimuer (Basidiomycota, Fungi), the third most important cultivated mushroom worldwide
human: Heimuer, Auricularia heimuer, is one of the most famous traditional Chinese foods and medicines, and it is the third most important cultivated mushroom worldwide. The aim of this study is to develop genomic resources for A. heimuer to furnish tools that can be used to study its secondary metabolite production capability, wood degradation ability and biosynthesis of polysaccharides. The genome was obtained from single spore mycelia of the strain Dai 13782 by using combined high-throughput Illumina HiSeq 4000 system with the PacBio RSII long-read sequencing platform. Functional annotation was accomplished by blasting protein sequences with different public available databases to obtain their corresponding annotations. It is 49.76Mb in size with a N50 scaffold size of 1,350,668bp and encodes 16,244 putative predicted genes. This is the first genome-scale assembly and annotation for A. heimuer, which is the third sequenced species in Auricularia.
text: Heimuer (*Auricularia heimuer*) is one of the most renowned traditional Chinese foods and medicinal fungi—and the third most widely cultivated mushroom globally. This study aimed to generate high-quality genomic resources for *A. heimuer* to support research into its capacity for secondary metabolite production, lignocellulose degradation, and polysaccharide biosynthesis. The genome was sequenced from single-spore isolates of strain Dai 13782 using a hybrid approach combining Illumina HiSeq 4000 short-read and PacBio RSII long-read technologies. Functional annotation was performed by BLAST-based alignment of predicted protein sequences against multiple public databases. The assembled genome spans 49.76 Mb, with an N50 scaffold length of 1,350,668 bp, and encodes 16,244 predicted protein-coding genes. This represents the first genome-scale assembly and annotation for *A. heimuer*, and the third sequenced species within the genus *Auricularia*.

The movie opens with a flashback to Doddsville County High School on April Fool's Day. A group of students play a prank on class nerd Marty. When they are punished for playing said prank, they follow up with a bigger prank which (par for the course in slasher films involving pranks on class nerds) goes ridiculously awry leaving Marty simultaneously burned by fire and disfigured by acid for the sake of being thorough. Fast forward five years, where we find members of the student body gathering at the now abandoned high school for their five year class reunion. We find out that it is no coincidence that everyone at the reunion belonged to the clique of pranksters from the flashback scene, as all of the attendees are being stalked and killed by a mysterious, jester mask-clad murderer in increasingly complicated and mind-numbingly ludicrous fashions. It doesn't take Sherlock Holmes to solve the mystery of the killer's identity, as it is revealed to be none other than a scarred Marty who has seemingly been using his nerd rage and high intellect to bend the laws of physics and engineering in order to rig the school for his revenge scenario. The film takes a turn for the bizarre as Marty finishes exacting his revenge on his former tormentors, only to be haunted by their ghosts. Marty is finally pushed fully over the edge and takes his own life. Finally, the film explodes in a crescendo of disjointed weirdness as the whole revenge scenario is revealed to be a dream in the first place as Marty wakes up in a hospital bed, breaks free of his restraints, stabs a nurse, and finally disfigures his own face.

The script is tired and suffers from a terminal case of horror movie logic. The only originality comes from the mind-numbingly convoluted ways that the victims are dispatched. The absurd it-was-all-a-dream ending feels tacked on. It's almost as if someone pointed out the disjointed nature of the film and the writer decided then and there that it was a dream.

Technically speaking, the film is atrocious. Some scenes were filmed so dark that I had to pause the film and play with the color on my television. The acting is sub-par, even for slasher films. I can't help but think that casting was a part of the problem as all of the actors look at least five years older than the characters they portray, which makes the flashback scene even more unintentionally laughable. Their lack of commitment to the movie is made obvious as half of them can't bother to keep their accents straight through the movie.

All of this being said, if you like bad horror movies, you might like this one, too. It isn't the worst film of the genre, but it's far from the best.
text:
The film opens with a flashback to Doddsville County High School on April Fool’s Day, where a group of students targets class outcast Marty with a prank. After receiving disciplinary consequences, they escalate with a far more elaborate stunt—one that, in keeping with slasher-film convention, spirals catastrophically out of control: Marty is both severely burned and disfigured by acid in a single, grotesquely over-engineered incident.  

Five years later, the same group reunites at the now-abandoned high school for their class reunion—only to discover that their gathering is no coincidence. Each attendee was part of the original prank clique, and all are now being hunted and murdered in increasingly baroque, implausible, and darkly inventive ways by a masked killer wearing a jester’s costume. The identity of the assailant is revealed early: it’s Marty, physically scarred and psychologically shattered, who has leveraged his intellect—and an improbable command of physics and engineering—to transform the derelict building into an elaborate death trap for his former tormentors.  

After completing his vengeance, the narrative takes a surreal turn: Marty is haunted by the ghosts of his victims, driving him irrevocably toward madness and, ultimately, suicide. The film then pivots once more—into outright absurdity—as the entire revenge sequence is exposed as a dream. Marty awakens in a hospital bed, breaks free from restraints, stabs a nurse, and deliberately disfigures his own face.  

The screenplay suffers from exhausted genre tropes and pervasive lapses in internal logic—the hallmark of “horror movie logic.” Its sole distinguishing feature is the sheer convolution of its kill sequences, though even these feel less inventive than exhausting. The dream-reveal ending lands as contrived and unearned, appearing less like a deliberate narrative choice and more like a last-minute attempt to rationalize the film’s structural incoherence.  

Technically, the production is deeply flawed. Several scenes are so poorly lit that viewers may need to adjust display settings mid-screening. Acting is uniformly weak—even by slasher-film standards—with inconsistent accents and a palpable lack of engagement from the cast. Age-inappropriate casting further undermines credibility: nearly every actor appears significantly older than their character’s stated age, rendering the opening flashback unintentionally comical.  

That said, fans of so-bad-it’s-good horror may find a certain perverse appeal here. It is neither the worst nor the best entry in the genre—but it is undeniably, unapologetically, and exhaustingly *of* it.

title: Who is a good neighbor? Analysis of frontrunner cities with comparative advantages in low-carbon development
human: A well-developed economy and low-carbon emission intensity are important characteristics of low-carbon cities; they also represent important tasks for achieving global climate change mitigation goals. It is seldom discussed, however, how we should identify frontrunner cities from which low-carbon development experiences can be gleaned and then implemented in neighboring cities. This study, therefore, proposed a simple indicator-the "good neighbor index"-to identify frontrunner cities in low-carbon transformation based on economic and emission performance. Based on this indicator, we identified "good neighbors" in static and dynamic views for China. The results showed that the static good neighbors in 2015 were mostly large cities with higher incomes and better industrial structures whereas the dynamic neighbors achieved better economic growth and emission reductions from 2005 to 2015, though their economic and emissions statuses were generally worse. The good neighbor list is not consistent with the list of national low-carbon pilot cities, which has largely overlooked the experiences of some fast-growing cities. These results have policy implications for the Chinese government in terms of promoting the low-carbon transformation of cities. The study can also provide a reference for other countries in addressing climate change at the city level.
text: A well-developed economy and low carbon emission intensity are hallmarks of low-carbon cities—and critical levers for achieving global climate mitigation targets. Yet, how to systematically identify frontrunner cities whose low-carbon development experiences can be effectively shared and scaled across neighboring urban areas remains underexplored. To address this gap, this study introduces a simple yet practical metric—the “Good Neighbor Index”—designed to identify frontrunner cities in low-carbon transformation based on integrated assessments of economic performance and emissions outcomes. Applying this index, we identify “Good Neighbors” in both static (cross-sectional) and dynamic (longitudinal) terms for China. Our analysis reveals that static Good Neighbors in 2015 were predominantly large, high-income cities with relatively advanced industrial structures; by contrast, dynamic Good Neighbors—those achieving the strongest simultaneous gains in economic growth and emissions reduction between 2005 and 2015—tended to start from lower baseline levels of economic development and higher emissions intensities. Notably, the resulting Good Neighbor list diverges significantly from China’s official national low-carbon pilot city roster, which has largely overlooked the valuable lessons emerging from rapidly transforming cities. These findings offer actionable insights for Chinese policymakers seeking to accelerate and broaden urban low-carbon transitions. Moreover, the conceptual framework and methodology presented here may serve as a useful reference for other countries pursuing climate action at the city level.

title: Effects of an evidence-based nursing intervention on prevention of anxiety and depression in the postpartum period
human: Postpartum depression has been one of the most common psychological disorders in patients during postpartum period. The constant anxiety and depression during this period seriously affect the physiological and psychological health of both the mother and infant. Evidence-based nursing has been widely applied in clinical practice and has achieved remarkable results. However, the effect of evidence-based nursing on postpartum depression remains unclear. Pregnant women who were not diagnosed with postpartum depression during hospitalisation (Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale [EPDS] ≤ 13 points) but prone to postpartum depression (EPDS scores of 9-13) were recruited into the study. They were randomly divided into the Intervention group (N = 60) and Control group (N = 60). Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD), Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAMA), EPDS and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) were used to investigate the psychological outcomes of puerperae during and after the 6-week intervention. Both the intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses showed that 6 weeks of evidence-based nursing intervention significantly reduced the incidence of postpartum depression. The application of the evidence-based nursing also improved the patients' satisfaction degree and effectively alleviated their anxiety according to both the intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses. Evidence-based nursing intervention had positive effects against anxiety and depression in the postpartum period.
text: Postpartum depression is among the most prevalent psychological disorders affecting women during the postpartum period. Persistent anxiety and depressive symptoms during this time significantly impair both maternal and infant physiological and psychological well-being. Although evidence-based nursing is widely implemented in clinical practice—and has demonstrated substantial benefits—the specific impact of such interventions on postpartum depression remains uncertain. This study enrolled pregnant women who were not diagnosed with postpartum depression during hospitalisation (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale [EPDS] score ≤13) but were at elevated risk (EPDS scores 9–13). Participants were randomly assigned to either an Intervention group (n = 60) or a Control group (n = 60). Psychological outcomes—including depression (HAMD), anxiety (HAMA), postpartum depression (EPDS), and sleep quality (PSQI)—were assessed during and at the conclusion of a 6-week intervention. Both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses revealed that the 6-week evidence-based nursing intervention significantly reduced the incidence of postpartum depression. Additionally, the intervention improved patient satisfaction and effectively alleviated anxiety—findings consistent across both analytical approaches. Overall, evidence-based nursing demonstrated clear benefits for mitigating anxiety and depression in the postpartum period.

title: Induction, identification and characterization of tetraploidy in Lycium ruthenicum
human: Lycium ruthenicum of Solanaceae was widely used as healthy vegetables and natural medicine foods for containing numerous functional components in leaves, roots and fruits. In the present study, tetraploid plants of L. ruthenicum were obtained efficiently by treating their leaves with colchicine in vitro. The highest induction frequency of the tetraploids was 31.4%, which was obtained by preculturing the leaves for 10 days and then treating them with 100 mg/L of colchicine concentration for 48 h. The ploidy levels of the regenerated plants were determined by flow cytometry and chromosome counting methods. Cytological, morphological, and histological characterization validated the results of flow cytometry, revealing the differences between the two kinds of ploidy plants in their tissue culture stage and field production stages. Morphological indexes also provide a simple and intuitionistic method for distinguishing tetraploid from diploid plants. As the chromosome number increased, the stomatal size and number of the chloroplasts in the stomata also increased, but the stomatal density decreased. The results indicate that the chromosome number is correlated with the stomatal index. The generated tetraploid is a potentially useful cultivated variety and will be beneficial for producing triploid progeny in the future.
text: *Lycium ruthenicum* (family Solanaceae) is widely valued as both a nutritious vegetable and a functional food with medicinal properties, owing to its rich content of bioactive compounds in leaves, roots, and fruits. In this study, tetraploid *L. ruthenicum* plants were efficiently induced *in vitro* via colchicine treatment of leaf explants. The optimal protocol—comprising a 10-day preculture followed by a 48-hour exposure to 100 mg/L colchicine—achieved a maximum tetraploid induction frequency of 31.4%. Ploidy levels of regenerated plants were confirmed using flow cytometry and chromosome counting. Complementary cytological, morphological, and histological analyses validated the ploidy assessments and revealed consistent phenotypic distinctions between diploid and tetraploid lines across both tissue culture and field-grown stages. Morphological traits—including stomatal size, chloroplast number per stoma, and stomatal density—proved reliable, intuitive indicators for rapid ploidy identification. Specifically, tetraploids exhibited significantly larger stomata and greater chloroplast numbers per stoma, but reduced stomatal density, indicating a strong correlation between ploidy level and stomatal index. These findings demonstrate that the newly generated tetraploid line holds considerable potential as an improved cultivated variety and serves as a valuable genetic resource for future breeding—particularly for the production of triploid progeny.

title: Deep-Resp-Forest: A deep forest model to predict anti-cancer drug response
human: The identification of therapeutic biomarkers predictive of drug response is crucial in personalized medicine. A number of computational models to predict response of anti-cancer drugs have been developed as the establishment of several pharmacogenomics screening databases. In our study, we proposed a deep cascaded forest model, Deep-Resp-Forest, to classify the anti-cancer drug response as "sensitive" or "resistant". We made three contributions in this study. Firstly, diverse molecular data could be effectively integrated to provide more information than single type of data for the classification. Combination of two types of data were tested here. Secondly, two structures based on the multi-grained scanning to transform the raw features into high-dimensional feature vectors and integrate the diverse data were proposed in our study. Thirdly, the original deep and time-consuming architecture of cascade forest was improved by a feature optimization operation, which emphasized the most discriminative features across layers. We evaluated the proposed method on the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE) and Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC) data sets and then compared with the Support Vector Machine. The proposed Deep-Resp-Forest has demonstrated the promising use of deep learning and deep forest approach on the drug response prediction tasks. The R implementation for running our experiments is available athttps://github.com/RanSuLab/Deep-Resp-Forest.
text: Identifying therapeutic biomarkers that predict drug response is essential for advancing personalized medicine. With the emergence of several pharmacogenomics screening databases, numerous computational models have been developed to predict anticancer drug responses. In this study, we propose Deep-Resp-Forest—a deep cascaded forest model designed to classify cancer cell lines as either “sensitive” or “resistant” to a given anticancer drug. Our work makes three key contributions: First, we demonstrate that integrating diverse molecular data types yields richer predictive information than any single data modality alone; specifically, we evaluate combinations of two complementary data types. Second, we introduce two novel multi-grained scanning–based architectures to transform raw molecular features into high-dimensional representations and effectively fuse heterogeneous data sources. Third, we enhance the original deep cascaded forest framework by incorporating a feature optimization step that progressively emphasizes the most discriminative features across hierarchical layers—thereby improving both efficiency and predictive performance. We rigorously evaluate Deep-Resp-Forest on two widely used benchmark datasets—the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE) and the Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC)—and compare its performance against Support Vector Machine (SVM). Results show that Deep-Resp-Forest achieves competitive accuracy while highlighting the promise of deep forest architectures in drug response prediction. The R implementation used in this study is publicly available at https://github.com/RanSuLab/Deep-Resp-Forest.

text:
A fisherman hunting for kingfish off Sydney Harbour got more than he bargained for when he hauled a four-metre bull shark from the water.  

Damon Smith-Horak was fishing last week about 500 metres off Watson’s Bay when he hooked the massive predator—weighing an estimated 200 kg. It took him over two hours to land the 10½-foot shark.  

Speaking to Nine News, Smith-Horak described it as the largest bull shark he’d ever seen. “It’s the biggest bull shark I’ve ever seen—it was about 10½ feet long,” he said.  

Though Sydney Harbour is best known as a haven for sunbathers, this wasn’t Smith-Horak’s first encounter with a shark. In fact, the four-metre bull was the third shark to take his bait that day—but the only one he successfully landed.  

He captured the entire struggle on video, showing the experienced angler reeling in the enormous animal using little more than a standard fishing rod. In the footage, the cameraman appears visibly wary as the shark approaches the boat, joking, “It’s going to eat the boat.” Fortunately, it didn’t—and the men safely brought the shark ashore.  

Smith-Horak views its presence in the harbour as a positive sign. “It’s actually a good sign—it just goes to show how much we’ve cleaned up our harbours,” he told Nine News.  

The video emerges as NSW Premier Mike Baird announces a $100,000 trial of shark-detecting sonar technology. The system will undergo rigorous testing at an aquarium before potential deployment. The initiative follows disturbing underwater footage revealing that many of the shark nets along NSW beaches contain large gaps—“easily big enough for a shark to pass through,” according to reports.  

“The expectation is that, once deployed, the sonar will detect sharks near beaches and instantly alert lifesavers on shore—enabling early warnings and rapid response,” Premier Baird said Sunday.

title: Tillage and seeding strategies for wheat optimizing production in harvested rice fields with high soil moisture
human: Suitable tillage and seeding strategies for wheat can be used to combat excessive residues and poor soil conditions in harvested rice fields. This study investigated the effects of different tillage (zero tillage and rotary tillage) and seeding methods on wheat growth, grain yield, nitrogen (N) uptake and utilization, and economic benefit when the soil moisture was high during the tillage and seeding practices. In 2016-2017, three seeders were tested: SM1-1, SM2, and SM3; in 2017-2018, four seeders were tested: SM1-2, SM2, SM3, and SM4. Although the soil moisture was different between years, zero tillage could be used to reduce the sowing depth, which facilitated early-phase wheat growth and N uptake compared with rotary tillage, resulting in higher grain yield, NUpE, and net return. In 2016-2017 (high wet soil), a small-size seeder (SM1-1) with sowing near the soil surface facilitated higher grain yield, NUpE, and net returns compared with the other seeders; in 2017-2018 (low wet soil), medium-size seeders (SM3 and SM4) were more suitable than small-size seeders (SM1-2 and SM2). In both years, the seeders that performed the best mainly improved the spike numbers while increasing N uptake, especially after anthesis. Zero tillage lowered input costs, but small-size seeders did not reduce costs due to the higher labor costs associated with their low working efficiency. Improving net returns depends largely on increasing yield. In conclusion, zero tillage is recommended for wheat production in harvested rice fields with a high soil moisture content, but the suitable seeding method needs to be confirmed according to the soil moisture content.
text:
This study evaluated tillage and seeding strategies for wheat cultivation in rice-harvested fields characterized by excessive crop residue and suboptimal soil conditions. Specifically, it assessed the effects of two tillage systems—zero tillage and rotary tillage—and various seeding methods on wheat growth, grain yield, nitrogen (N) uptake and utilization efficiency (NUpE), and economic returns under high soil moisture conditions during sowing. Field trials were conducted over two growing seasons: in 2016–2017, three seeders (SM1-1, SM2, SM3) were evaluated; in 2017–2018, four seeders (SM1-2, SM2, SM3, SM4) were tested. Although soil moisture levels differed between years—higher in 2016–2017 and lower in 2017–2018—zero tillage consistently reduced sowing depth compared with rotary tillage, thereby promoting earlier crop establishment, enhanced early-season N uptake, higher grain yield, improved NUpE, and greater net returns.  

In the wetter 2016–2017 season, the small-sized seeder SM1-1—designed for shallow, surface-near sowing—outperformed the others in terms of grain yield, NUpE, and net returns. In contrast, during the drier 2017–2018 season, medium-sized seeders (SM3 and SM4) proved more effective than the smaller models (SM1-2 and SM2). Across both years, top-performing seeders primarily increased yield by boosting spike number while also enhancing post-anthesis N uptake. Economically, zero tillage lowered input costs, whereas small-sized seeders did not reduce overall costs due to their lower operational efficiency and associated higher labor requirements. Net returns were found to depend predominantly on yield gains.  

In summary, zero tillage is recommended for wheat production in rice-fallow fields with high soil moisture at sowing; however, the optimal seeding method must be selected based on prevailing soil moisture conditions.

text:
The most widely circulated objection to the proposed Constitution—particularly in this State, and likely in several others—is its alleged failure to guarantee the right to trial by jury in civil cases. Though the disingenuous framing of this objection has been repeatedly identified and refuted, it persists unabated in the speeches and writings of the Constitution’s opponents. The Constitution’s mere silence on civil trials is misrepresented as an outright abolition of jury trials—and the rhetoric built upon this misrepresentation is carefully crafted to foster the false impression that this supposed abolition is absolute and universal, extending not only to all categories of civil litigation but even to criminal cases. Yet to argue against such a claim in the criminal context would be as futile as attempting to prove the existence of matter itself—or to demonstrate, through formal argument, any proposition whose truth is self-evident once clearly expressed.

With regard to civil cases, proponents of this fallacy have resorted to sophistries so flimsy they scarcely merit refutation: namely, that the absence of an explicit constitutional provision for civil jury trials amounts to their total elimination. Any thoughtful observer immediately recognizes the vast gulf between silence and abolition. Still, because those advancing this misreading have attempted to cloak it in the language of established legal maxims—distorting their original meaning—it may be worthwhile to examine the ground they purport to occupy.

The maxims they invoke are familiar ones: “A specification of particulars implies the exclusion of generals,” or “The expression of one thing implies the exclusion of another.” From this, they conclude that, since the Constitution expressly guarantees jury trials in criminal cases while remaining silent on civil ones, that silence must constitute an implied prohibition against jury trials in civil matters.

Legal interpretive rules are, at bottom, codifications of common sense—adopted by courts to ascertain legislative intent in statutory construction. Their proper application, therefore, must align with the sound reasoning from which they originate. Bearing this in mind, consider: Is it reasonable to suppose that a constitutional requirement obliging the legislature to assign criminal trials to juries thereby strips it of the authority to permit or authorize jury trials in other contexts? Is it natural to infer that a command to perform one act constitutes a prohibition against performing another—especially when that other act was previously within the legislature’s power and is wholly compatible with the mandated action? If such an inference is inherently unnatural and unreasonable, then it cannot be rational to maintain that a constitutional injunction requiring jury trials in certain cases operates as a blanket interdiction against them elsewhere.

The power to establish courts necessarily includes the power to prescribe the mode of trial. In the absence of any constitutional directive on juries, the legislature would retain full discretion—to adopt the jury system or to forgo it entirely. That discretion is curtailed in criminal cases by the Constitution’s explicit mandate; but with respect to civil cases—on which the document is wholly silent—the legislature’s discretion remains unfettered. To specify a duty to employ juries in criminal trials excludes, to be sure, any corresponding duty (or necessity) to do so in civil cases—but it does not constrain the legislature’s authority to employ them there if it deems such a course advisable. The claim, therefore, that the national legislature would lack full authority to submit all federal civil cases to jury determination rests on no sound foundation whatsoever.

From these considerations, the following conclusion follows inexorably: trial by jury in civil cases would not be abolished; and the effort to portray the Constitution’s silence as tantamount to abolition is without merit.

title: Proteomic analysis in kidneys of Atlantic salmon infected with Aeromonas salmonicida by iTRAQ
human: Aeromonas salmonicida is a major etiologic agent which induces furunculosis and is globally harmful in salmonid and turbot cultures, especially in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) farming. In order to improve knowledge of its poorly understood pathogenesis, we utilized high-throughput proteomics to display differentially expressed proteins in the kidney of Atlantic salmon challenged with high and low infection dose of A. salmonicida at 7 and 14 days. In quantitative proteomic assays, isobaric tags for relative and absolute quantitation (iTRAQ) combined with 2D LC-MS/MS is emerging as a powerful methodology in the search for disease-specific targets and biomarkers. In this study, 4009 distinct proteins (unused ≥ 1.3, which is a confidence ≥ 95%) were identified in three two-dimensional LC/MS/MS analyses. Then we chose 140 proteins (fold change ratio ≥ 1.5 and P < 0.01) combined with protein-protein interaction analysis to ultimately obtain 39 proteins in network which could be considered as potential biomarkers for Atlantic salmon immune responses. Nine significant differentially expressed proteins were consistent with those at the proteomic level used to validate genes at the transcriptomic level by qPCR. Collectively, these data was first reported using an iTRAQ approach to provide additional elements for consideration in the pathophysiology of A. salmonicida and pave the way to resolve the influence of this disease in Atlantic salmon.

title: Chronic Illness and Income Diversification in Rural China
human: Off-farm diversification offers an important pathway out of poverty while health-impaired rural farmers can hardly seize the opportunity in developing countries. This paper investigates how chronic illness shapes livelihood structure and income generation in rural China. Our sample consists of 3850 rural households in Southern China and we rely on instrumental variable regressions to identify causal effects. We find that farmers with chronic illness tend to diversify towards local off-farm employments, rather than migrants, since local off-farm employments are more likely to act in a strategically complementary way to farming. Further analysis shows that income returns of diversification tend to be substantially higher for the health-impaired. While the relationship between diversification and income presents a conventional inverted U shape for the healthy, it is best categorized as upward sloping with diminishing marginal effects for farmers with chronic illness.
text: Off-farm diversification is a vital pathway out of poverty—yet rural farmers with health impairments in developing countries often struggle to access this opportunity. This paper examines how chronic illness affects livelihood structure and income generation among rural households in China. Drawing on a survey of 3,850 rural households in southern China, we use instrumental variable regressions to identify causal effects. We find that chronically ill farmers are more likely to diversify into local off-farm employment than into migration, as such local opportunities complement farming activities more strategically. Further analysis reveals that income returns from diversification are substantially higher for health-impaired farmers. Whereas the relationship between diversification and income follows a conventional inverted-U pattern for healthy farmers, it is upward-sloping—with diminishing marginal returns—for those with chronic illness.

text:
After just two years of operations in Canada, Target Corporation has announced its complete withdrawal from the Canadian market, citing sustained and substantial financial losses—reaching nearly $1 billion annually. The decision will result in the closure of all 133 Canadian stores and the eventual termination of employment for approximately 17,600 associates.

Brian Cornell, Chairman and CEO of Target Corp., announced the move on Thursday—the first major strategic action since assuming the CEO role in August. In a statement posted on the company’s corporate blog, Cornell acknowledged that Target Canada had failed to achieve the performance improvements anticipated over the critical holiday period, despite earlier progress in pricing strategy and product assortment. He noted that while Canadian consumers were already familiar with and favorably disposed toward the Target brand—many having shopped at U.S. locations—the company “missed the mark from the beginning by taking on too much too fast.” Operational challenges—including inventory mismanagement, inconsistent pricing, and an overall customer experience that fell short of both guest expectations and Target’s own standards—proved persistent and insurmountable.

Cornell confirmed that the company sees no realistic path to profitability for its Canadian operations before at least 2021. Target’s difficulties in Canada reflect broader challenges faced by several U.S.-based retailers entering or expanding in the Canadian market: Best Buy Co., Big Lots Inc., and Walmart Stores Inc. have all scaled back or weakened their Canadian presence amid regulatory complexity, economic headwinds, and intensifying competition.

Financially, Target expects fourth-quarter losses of approximately $5.4 billion related to discontinued Canadian operations, with an additional $275 million in losses anticipated on discontinued operations in fiscal 2015. Exit-related cash costs are projected to total between $500 million and $600 million, predominantly incurred in fiscal 2015 or later. Target affirmed it holds sufficient liquidity to fund these obligations. As part of its wind-down plan, the company has received court approval to voluntarily contribute approximately $59 million into an employee trust. Once finalized, the trust is expected to provide nearly all Canadian employees—including those not required through the full liquidation process—with a minimum of 16 weeks of compensation, covering wages and benefits.

Canadian stores will remain open during the liquidation phase. Target anticipates that exiting Canada will enhance earnings beginning in fiscal 2015 and improve cash flow starting in fiscal 2016. Concurrently, the company revised its U.S. outlook upward: same-store sales (for U.S. stores open at least one year) are now projected to increase approximately 3% in the fourth quarter—up from a prior forecast of 2%. This improvement reflects stronger-than-expected traffic and online sales during November and December. Same-store sales remain a key indicator of retail health, as they exclude results from newly opened or recently closed locations. Target also raised its fourth-quarter adjusted earnings guidance to $1.43–$1.47 per share. Following the announcement, Target’s stock rose $2.66, or 3.6%, to $76.99 before market open.

It is best to pay in your land a skillful gardener, or to buy good sense applied to gardening; in your sailor, good sense applied to navigation; in the house, good sense applied to cooking, sewing, serving; in your agent, good sense applied to accounts and affairs. The thief steals from himself. The swindler swindles himself. For the real price of labor is knowledge and virtue, whereof wealth and credit are signs. These signs, like paper money, may be counterfeited or stolen, but that which they represent, namely, knowledge and virtue, cannot be counterfeited or stolen. These ends of labor cannot be answered but by real exertions of the mind, and in obedience to pure motives. The cheat, the defaulter, the gambler, cannot extort the knowledge of material and moral nature which his honest care and pains yield to the operative. Labor, too, is governed by the same unrelenting laws. “The cheapest labor,” the prudent declare, “is the dearest.” What we purchase in a broom, a mat, a wagon, or a knife is not merely an object—but the application of sound judgment to a common need. It is wisest, therefore, to pay for skillful gardening—whether by hiring a gardener versed in the craft or by acquiring the practical wisdom that gardening embodies; for expert seamanship, whether through a seasoned sailor or the distilled intelligence of navigation; for domestic excellence—whether in cooking, sewing, or service—by investing in the discernment those arts require; and for sound stewardship—whether through a trusted agent or by cultivating the judgment needed for accounts and affairs. In this way, you extend your presence, multiplying your influence across your entire domain.

Yet because reality rests upon a dual constitution—both moral and material—there can be no deception in labor, any more than in life itself. The thief steals from himself; the swindler defrauds himself. For the true cost of labor is knowledge and virtue—of which wealth and credit are but outward signs. Like paper money, these signs may be counterfeited or stolen; but the realities they signify—knowledge and virtue—cannot be forged or taken. These ends of labor cannot be achieved except through genuine mental effort and in obedience to pure motives. The cheat, the defaulter, the gambler, cannot compel from nature the insight into material and moral law that honest diligence and sustained effort yield to the conscientious worker. Nature’s law is clear: *Do the thing—and you shall gain the power.* Those who omit the doing forfeit the power.

The alliance between virtue and nature ensures that all things conspire against vice. The world’s beautiful laws and elemental substances—water, wind, snow, gravity—turn hostile toward the traitor. He discovers that creation is ordered for truth and benefit alone—and that there is no hiding place, no sanctuary, anywhere on earth for the rogue. Commit a crime, and the earth becomes glass—transparent, revealing all. Commit a crime, and it is as if a fresh fall of snow blankets the ground: in the woods, every partridge, fox, squirrel, and mole leaves its unmistakable track. You cannot recall a spoken word; you cannot erase a footprint; you cannot draw up the ladder so completely as to leave no trace, no clue. Some damning circumstance always emerges. Nature’s very elements—water, snow, wind, gravitation—become instruments of retribution for the thief.

Conversely, the same law holds with equal certainty for every right action. Love—and you shall be loved. All love is mathematically just, as rigorously balanced as the two sides of an algebraic equation. The good person possesses absolute good—a force as transformative as fire, converting everything it touches to its own nature. Thus, no harm can truly be done to him. Just as Napoleon’s royal adversaries, upon his approach, cast down their banners and turned from foes to friends, so too do calamities—sickness, insult, poverty—reveal themselves, in time, as benefactors.

Even weakness and defect befriend the good. As no man ever possessed a point of pride that did not ultimately injure him, so no man ever bore a defect that was not, somewhere and somehow, turned to his advantage. In the fable, the stag admired his majestic horns but scorned his feet—until the hunter came: then his feet saved him; later, caught in the thicket, his horns ensnared him. Every person, in the course of life, must one day thank his faults. As no one fully grasps a truth until he has wrestled with it, so no one gains intimate knowledge of human limitations—or of human capacities—until he has suffered under the former and witnessed the latter triumph over his own lack. Does he possess a temper so volatile it renders him unfit for society? Then he is driven inward—to solitude, to self-reliance, to habits of resourcefulness—until, like the wounded oyster, he seals his wound with pearl.

Our strength arises from our weakness. Indignation armed with hidden reserves does not stir until we are pricked, stung, and sorely tested. A great man is always willing to be small. While seated comfortably upon the cushions of privilege, he grows drowsy. But when punished, tormented, or defeated—he awakens. He is thrown back upon his wits, upon his manhood. He gains facts; he learns the extent of his ignorance; he is cured of the delusion of self-sufficiency; he acquires moderation and genuine skill.

title: Brain morphological changes in hypokinetic dysarthria of Parkinson's disease and use of machine learning to predict severity
human: Up to 90% of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) eventually develop the speech and voice disorder referred to as hypokinetic dysarthria (HD). However, the brain morphological changes associated with HD have not been investigated. Moreover, no reliable model for predicting the severity of HD based on neuroimaging has yet been developed. A total of 134 PD patients were included in this study and divided into a training set and a test set. All participants underwent a structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan and neuropsychological evaluation. Individual cortical thickness, subcortical structure, and white matter volume were extracted, and their association with HD severity was analyzed. After feature selection, a machine-learning model was established using a support vector machine in the training set. The severity of HD was then predicted in the test set. Atrophy of the right precentral cortex and the right fusiform gyrus was significantly associated with HD. No association was found between HD and volume of white matter or subcortical structures. Favorable and optimal performance of machine learning on HD severity prediction was achieved using feature selection, giving a correlation coefficient (r) of .7516 and a coefficient of determination (R2 ) of .5649 (P < .001). The brain morphological changes were associated with HD. Excellent prediction of the severity of HD was achieved using machine learning based on neuroimaging.

text:
By Ashley Collman for MailOnline  

The parents of executed journalist James Foley revealed they shared their grief with “kind and dear” Pope Francis when he called them at their New Hampshire home from the Vatican on Thursday.  

Diane and John Foley said the pontiff’s words brought profound comfort as they grapple with the aftermath of their son’s brutal murder—broadcast globally by his ISIS captors on Tuesday.  

Though they did not disclose the details of their 20-minute conversation, the Foleys expressed deep gratitude that Pope Francis reached out—even as he mourned the recent deaths of his two young nephews and their mother in a car crash in Argentina; one nephew remains critically ill.  

“Pope Francis was so dear because he is grieving himself, having just lost three members of his family,” Diane Foley said during an appearance with her husband on the *Today* show. “In the midst of his tremendous grief, he took the time to call—and our whole family was there. My brother-in-law spoke to him in Spanish, and he was just so kind.”  

The Pope’s call—made amid global outrage over James Foley’s killing—left the devoutly Catholic Foleys “deeply moved and grateful.”  

“He offered us his personal prayers, and we felt truly comforted and supported,” John Foley said.  

The call came around 3 p.m. Thursday at the family’s home in Rochester, New Hampshire, with assistance from a translator. “He was very compassionate, very loving,” said Father Marc Montminy, pastor of St. Michael’s Church in Exeter, New Hampshire, and the Foley family’s priest.  

Pope Francis phoned the family of the slain American photojournalist to offer solace.  

The Foleys have been in mourning since Tuesday, when a video surfaced online showing James Foley’s horrific beheading by ISIS affiliates. He had been missing for two years after being kidnapped while reporting in Syria.  

On Wednesday, his grieving parents held a press conference outside their Rochester home—where a yellow ribbon hung on the front door.  

“We are very proud of Jim. He was a courageous, fearless journalist—the best of America,” Diane Foley said. “He was driven by the Syrian people’s deep desire for freedom and their suffering.”
