Recognize the Principles of the Judiciary Essay

Although the principles of judiciary demand the judicial process to follow due legal processes to the letter, legal crises do occur in some instances. Legal conflict arises when inconsistencies emerge between the constitution and the general laws.

A classical example is the Marbury v. Madison case of the United States in which a legal conflict arose due to the inconsistency of the United States constitution with the Judiciary Act. According to this case, “William Marbury petitioned the Supreme Court to compel James Madison, Secretary of State to effect his appointment as a commissioner of Justice for Peace in Columbia District but John Marshall, Chief Justice denied the petition as he termed it unconstitutional” (Reisman, 2007, p. 3).

This became a landmark ruling since the Supreme Court, for the first time in the United States history, declared an Act to be unconstitutional. In this ruling, John Marshal realized that there was legal conflict between the constitution and the Judicial Act, and the only way to conduct constitutional review was through the Supreme Court.

The Marbury v. Madison ruling coupled with some clauses in Article III authorizes the Supreme Court to carry out judicial review. The Article III of the United States constitution states that, “In all cases affecting ambassadors, other public ministers and consuls, and those in which a state shall be party, the Supreme Court shall have original jurisdiction…in all the other cases before mentioned, the Supreme Court shall have appellate jurisdiction” (Stone, 2007, p. 35).

Therefore, the United States constitution gives the powers to the Supreme Court to exercise judicial review in cases where legal conflict arises. The prime function of the Supreme Court in judicial review is to protect the constitution and ensure that all statutes are consistent with the constitution.

The constitutions of England and Netherland do not give powers to their Supreme Courts to exercise judicial review on the constitutionality of statues and treaties, because legislators have the mandate of ensuring that they only pass constitutional acts. In cases of constitutional dispute concerning “…the right interpretation of a law or a treaty in accordance with the constitution … the judge cannot have supremacy over the legislator, because the question of constitutionality of an act is more political than technical-judicial” (Huq, 2008, p. 32).

Halsema proposal seeks to have the Supreme Court assume the jurisdiction to check constitutionality of statutes and treaties. The approval of the Halsema proposal means that the parliament and the government will have to share their mandate of constitutional review with the judiciary, hence judicial review.

Most Americans accept judicial review even though it is not explicit in the constitution because it has provided means of checking constitutionality of statutes. Statistics shows that, “in the two hundred years of judicial review 175 federal laws and 1006 state laws were declared unconstitutional (1789-2004)” (Whittington, 2009, p. 12).

This means that if there was no judicial review, the courts could still be grappling with over 1000 legal conflicts, which slows down the wheels of justice. The landmark ruling of the Marbury v. Madison case set precedent on ways of solving legal conflicts that emerge quite often due to the inconsistencies of the statutes with the constitution.

Despite the fact that judicial review has helped to speed up the due process of the law, Thomas Jefferson criticized it saying that, “to consider judges as the ultimate arbiters of all constitutional questions is a very dangerous doctrine indeed, and one which would place us under the despotism of an oligarchy” (Reisman, 2007, p. 8).

Jefferson argues that judges are common people with same passions and interests that might lead them to make compromised judicial reviews to attain their desired ends. I agree with Jefferson
text:
The Principle of Judicial Review: A Comparative and Historical Analysis  

Judicial review—the authority of courts to assess the constitutionality of statutes and treaties—is a cornerstone of constitutional governance in certain legal systems, though its scope and legitimacy vary significantly across jurisdictions. While judicial independence and adherence to due process are fundamental principles of the judiciary, legal conflicts inevitably arise when statutory provisions or executive actions conflict with constitutional norms. Such conflicts present critical challenges to the rule of law and demand a clear institutional mechanism for resolution.

A pivotal moment in the development of judicial review occurred in *Marbury v. Madison* (1803), a landmark decision by the U.S. Supreme Court. In this case, William Marbury petitioned the Court to compel Secretary of State James Madison to deliver his commission as Justice of the Peace for the District of Columbia. Chief Justice John Marshall, while acknowledging Marbury’s legal entitlement, denied the writ of mandamus on constitutional grounds—holding that Section 13 of the Judiciary Act of 1789 unconstitutionally expanded the Court’s original jurisdiction beyond the limits prescribed by Article III of the U.S. Constitution (Reisman, 2007, p. 3). This ruling established, for the first time in American history, the principle that federal courts possess the authority—and indeed the duty—to invalidate laws inconsistent with the Constitution.

The decision was grounded not only in the facts of the case but also in the structural logic of Article III, which delineates the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction: “In all Cases affecting Ambassadors, other public Ministers and Consuls, and those in which a State shall be Party, the supreme Court shall have original Jurisdiction. In all the other Cases before mentioned, the supreme Court shall have appellate Jurisdiction” (Stone, 2007, p. 35). Marshall reasoned that where a statute contradicts the Constitution—a document of superior legal authority—the judiciary must uphold the Constitution as the supreme law of the land. Thus, *Marbury v. Madison* affirmed judicial review not as an explicit textual grant, but as an inherent function necessary to preserve constitutional supremacy and maintain the integrity of the separation of powers.

Consequently, the U.S. Supreme Court exercises judicial review as a core component of its constitutional role: safeguarding the Constitution and ensuring legislative and executive acts conform to its provisions. By contrast, constitutional frameworks in countries such as the United Kingdom and the Netherlands do not empower their highest courts to strike down statutes or treaties on constitutional grounds. There, constitutional compliance is entrusted primarily to the legislature; judges are expected to interpret laws in harmony with the constitution but lack authority to nullify them. As Huq (2008, p. 32) observes, “the question of constitutionality of an act is more political than technical-judicial,” and thus “the judge cannot have supremacy over the legislator” in determining the proper interpretation of law or treaty in light of constitutional principles.

In the Netherlands, recent proposals—including the Halsema initiative—have sought to confer constitutional review authority upon the Supreme Court, thereby shifting part of this responsibility from parliament and government to the judiciary. Adoption of such a reform would represent a significant departure from tradition, introducing formal judicial review into a system historically grounded in parliamentary sovereignty.

In the United States, judicial review enjoys broad acceptance despite its absence from the constitutional text. Its practical efficacy is evident in empirical data: between 1789 and 2004, the Supreme Court declared 175 federal statutes and 1,006 state laws unconstitutional (Whittington, 2009, p. 12). Absent this mechanism, courts would likely remain mired in protracted disputes arising from statutory-constitutional inconsistencies—impeding legal certainty and delaying justice. *Marbury v. Madison*, therefore, not only resolved an immediate legal conflict but also established a durable precedent for resolving such conflicts systematically and authoritatively.

Nevertheless, judicial review has long been subject to principled critique. Thomas Jefferson famously warned that vesting judges with “the ultimate arbiters of all constitutional questions” constitutes “a very dangerous doctrine indeed, and one which would place us under the despotism of an oligarchy” (Reisman, 2007, p. 8). His concern centered on the human fallibility of judges—their susceptibility to personal bias, political influence, and ideological predilection—which may compromise the objectivity and legitimacy of constitutional adjudication. This critique remains salient: while judicial review serves vital functions in constitutional democracies, its exercise demands rigorous accountability, transparency, and ongoing democratic scrutiny.

title: Dynamic evolution of cross-correlations in the Chinese stock market
human: The analysis of cross-correlations is extensively applied for the understanding of interconnections in stock markets and the portfolio risk estimation. Current studies of correlations in Chinese market mainly focus on the static correlations between return series, and this calls for an urgent need to investigate their dynamic correlations. Our study aims to reveal the dynamic evolution of cross-correlations in the Chinese stock market, and offer an exact interpretation for the evolution behavior. The correlation matrices constructed from the return series of 367 A-share stocks traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange from January 4, 1999 to December 30, 2011 are calculated over a moving window with a size of 400 days. The evolutions of the statistical properties of the correlation coefficients, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors of the correlation matrices are carefully analyzed. We find that the stock correlations are significantly increased in the periods of two market crashes in 2001 and 2008, during which only five eigenvalues significantly deviate from the random correlation matrix, and the systemic risk is higher in these volatile periods than calm periods. By investigating the significant contributors of the deviating eigenvectors in different time periods, we observe a dynamic evolution behavior in business sectors such as IT, electronics, and real estate, which lead the rise (drop) before (after) the crashes. Our results provide new perspectives for the understanding of the dynamic evolution of cross-correlations in the Chines stock markets, and the result of risk estimation is valuable for the application of risk management.
text:
Cross-correlation analysis is widely employed to uncover interdependencies among stocks and to estimate portfolio risk. While existing studies on the Chinese stock market have predominantly focused on static correlations between return series, there remains an urgent need to examine their dynamic behavior. This study investigates the time-varying nature of cross-correlations in the Chinese stock market and provides a precise interpretation of their evolutionary patterns.  

We construct correlation matrices from the daily returns of 367 A-share stocks listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange over the period January 4, 1999–December 30, 2011. These matrices are computed using a rolling window of 400 trading days. We systematically analyze the temporal evolution of key statistical properties—including correlation coefficients, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors—of these matrices.  

Our results reveal a marked increase in cross-correlations during the two major market crashes of 2001 and 2008. During these episodes, only five eigenvalues significantly deviate from those expected under a null random matrix model, indicating heightened systemic risk relative to more stable periods. Further, by identifying the dominant sectoral contributors to these deviating eigenvectors across time, we observe distinct dynamic patterns: sectors such as information technology, electronics, and real estate consistently lead the rise (and subsequent decline) in correlations preceding (and following) the crashes.  

These findings offer novel insights into the dynamic structure of cross-correlations in the Chinese stock market and yield practically valuable implications for risk estimation and management.

title: Dynamic Analyses of Contagion Risk and Module Evolution on the SSE A-Shares Market Based on Minimum Information Entropy
human: The interactive effect is significant in the Chinese stock market, exacerbating the abnormal market volatilities and risk contagion. Based on daily stock returns in the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) A-shares, this paper divides the period between 2005 and 2018 into eight bull and bear market stages to investigate interactive patterns in the Chinese financial market. We employ the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) method to construct the stock network, compare the heterogeneity of bull and bear markets, and further use the Map Equation method to analyse the evolution of modules in the SSE A-shares market. Empirical results show that (1) the connected effect is more significant in bear markets than bull markets and gives rise to abnormal volatilities in the stock market; (2) a system module can be found in the network during the first four stages, and the industry aggregation effect leads to module differentiation in the last four stages; (3) some stocks have leading effects on others throughout eight periods, and medium- and small-cap stocks with poor financial conditions are more likely to become risk sources, especially in bear markets. Our conclusions are beneficial to improving investment strategies and making regulatory policies.

text:
Opposition Leader Bill Shorten has renewed calls for Australia to become a republic, as campaigners continue to press for a new national flag—free of the Union Jack. “Let us have the courage to ask ourselves whether we aspire to more than a mere collection of clichés,” Mr. Shorten said.

Speaking on the eve of Australia Day at a book launch in Melbourne, the Labor leader urged Australians to reinvigorate the long-held vision of an Australian head of state. “Let us declare that our head of state should be one of us,” he said.

In his Australia Day address, Mr. Shorten called for a bold and inclusive national conversation: “Let us rally behind an Australian republic—a model that authentically reflects who we are, our modern identity, our place in the region, and our role in the world. Let us be brave enough to secure constitutional recognition for First Australians—and let us breathe new life into the dream of an Australian head of state.”

His remarks were welcomed by Geoff Gallop, Chair of the Australian Republican Movement, who acknowledged that advancing the cause remains challenging. “It’s hard work for us republicans—there’s no doubt about that,” Gallop told ABC Radio. “The failure of the 1999 referendum undoubtedly set the movement back.” He noted that current polling shows roughly one-third of Australians support an Australian head of state, one-third prefer retaining the monarchy, and the remainder remain undecided.

Gallop stressed that Australia’s Constitution is not fully independent: its head of state is determined by hereditary rules rooted in another nation’s history. “The great unifying step forward would be to commit to a proper, democratic process—one that engages the public meaningfully and determines, together, the best republican model for our future,” he said. “Those of us who believe must keep advocating. With every step forward, our confidence grows—and so does our nation.”

The push for a republic coincides with growing calls to redesign the Australian flag. Many argue the Union Jack should be removed—including journalist and commentator Derryn Hinch. “It should have been changed in 1988,” he told *Daily Mail Australia*. “I was living in Canada when it adopted the maple leaf flag—it was a defining moment for national pride. We should remove the Union Jack. What replaces it is for others to decide. The current flag emerged from a competition sponsored by a tobacco company—and I certainly don’t want to see a boxing kangaroo on the new design.”

TV presenter Ray Martin also advocates for a redesigned flag. Writing in *News.com.au*, he asked: “How many of our soldiers died fighting under those state flags? None. So why are those state flags still treated as untouchable? And what does our reluctance to change say about us—and our continued attachment to the symbolic ‘apron strings’ of England, more than a century after Federation?”

title: Genome-wide survey and expression analysis of the OSCA gene family in rice
human: Reception of and response to exogenous and endogenous osmotic changes is important to sustain plant growth and development, as well as reproductive formation. Hyperosmolality-gated calcium-permeable channels (OSCA) were first characterised as an osmosensor in Arabidopsis and are involved in the perception of extracellular changes to trigger hyperosmolality-induced [Ca(2+)]i increases (OICI). To explore the potential biological functions of OSCAs in rice, we performed a bioinformatics and expression analysis of the OsOSCA gene family. A total of 11 OsOSCA genes were identified from the genome database of Oryza sativa L. Japonica. Based on their sequence composition and phylogenetic relationship, the OsOSCA family was classified into four clades. Gene and protein structure analysis indicated that the 11 OsOSCAs shared similar structures with their homologs in Oryza sativa L. ssp. Indica, Oryza glaberrima, and Oryza brachyantha. Multiple sequence alignment analysis revealed a conserved DUF221 domain in these members, in which the first three TMs were conserved, while the others were not. The expression profiles of OsOSCA genes were analysed at different stages of vegetative growth, reproductive development, and under osmotic-associated abiotic stresses. We found that four and six OsOSCA genes showed a clear correlation between the expression profile and osmotic changes during caryopsis development and seed imbibition, respectively. Orchestrated transcription of three OsOSCAs was strongly associated with the circadian clock. Moreover, osmotic-related abiotic stress differentially induced the expression of 10 genes. The entire OSCA family is characterised by the presence of a conserved DUF221 domain, which functions as an osmotic-sensing calcium channel. The phylogenetic tree of OSCA genes showed that two subspecies of cultivated rice, Oryza sativa L. ssp. Japonica and Oryza sativa L. ssp. Indica, are more closely related than wild rice Oryza glaberrima, while Oryza brachyantha was less closely related. OsOSCA expression is organ- and tissue-specific and regulated by different osmotic-related abiotic stresses in rice. These findings will facilitate further research in this gene family and provide potential target genes for generation of genetically modified osmotic-stress-resistant plants.

title: Multi-layer information fusion based on graph convolutional network for knowledge-driven herb recommendation
human: Prescription of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is a precious treasure accumulated in the long-term development of TCM. Artificial intelligence (AI) technology is used to build herb recommendation models to deeply understand regularities in prescriptions, which is of great significance to clinical application of TCM and discovery of new prescriptions. Most of herb recommendation models constructed in the past ignored the nature information of herbs, and most of them used statistical models based on bag-of-words for herb recommendation, which makes it difficult for the model to perceive the complex correlation between symptoms and herbs. In this paper, we introduce the properties of herbs as additional auxiliary information by constructing herb knowledge graph, and propose a graph convolution model with multi-layer information fusion to obtain symptom feature representations and herb feature representations with rich information and less noise. We apply the proposed model to the TCM prescription dataset, and the experiment results show that our model outperforms the baseline models in terms of Precision@5 by 6.2%, Recall@5 by 16.0% and F1-Score@5 by 12.0%.
text: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) prescriptions represent a valuable legacy refined through centuries of clinical practice. Leveraging artificial intelligence (AI), researchers have developed herb recommendation models to uncover underlying patterns in prescription composition—advancing both clinical TCM practice and the discovery of novel prescriptions. However, most prior models overlooked herb properties (e.g., nature, taste, meridian affinity), relying instead on statistical bag-of-words approaches that struggle to capture the intricate relationships between symptoms and herbs. To address this, we incorporate herb properties as auxiliary knowledge via a purpose-built herb knowledge graph and propose a multi-layer graph convolutional model for fusing heterogeneous information. This enables robust, low-noise representations of both symptom and herb features. Evaluated on a real-world TCM prescription dataset, our model achieves improvements of 6.2% in Precision@5, 16.0% in Recall@5, and 12.0% in F1-Score@5 over baseline methods.

When the gods created humanity, they fashioned humankind as yet another earthly creature—walking the land and subsisting on its natural bounty. Yet humanity was distinct: crafted in the image of the immortals themselves, endowed with two arms and two legs like the Olympians. Though many deities failed to recognize this resemblance, others grew compassionate upon observing mortals from their celestial vantage—seeing reflections of themselves struggling through dense undergrowth and battling for survival.

Prometheus, the Titan known as the Trickster, Master of Forethought, and a former adversary turned turncoat in the Great War against the Olympians, felt profound empathy for humankind. He resolved to bestow upon them a divine gift—one only he could truly confer—to elevate them above all other mortal beings and establish their dominion over the earth. He weighed several possibilities: fire, his own faculty of forethought, or his brother Epimetheus’s gift of afterthought. Yet, drawing upon his mastery of foresight, he conceived a far more audacious and consequential plan.

He executed it in stages. First, he deceived Epimetheus into granting humanity fire and afterthought—while secretly endowing them with his own forethought. Prometheus anticipated Zeus’s wrath; he knew the king of the gods would fear humanity’s growing power—the very threat that had once led the Olympians to overthrow the Titans. And indeed, Zeus responded with fury, seeking to eradicate humankind entirely.

Even as Prometheus lay chained to his rocky torment, he smiled—not in defiance, but in quiet triumph. His greatest gift to humanity had not yet been revealed. It arrived in the form of Zeus’s own retribution: a cataclysmic flood that drowned the world and wiped out the beasts roaming the earth, intended as a violent reset. Yet this very wrath fulfilled Prometheus’s design. He had forewarned Deucalion—a just and wise man—and provided him with a massive chest in which to ride out the deluge. After nine days and nights, the waters receded. The earth emerged cleansed and renewed—and now, unchallenged, it belonged to humanity. When life returned, humans were already established as its sovereigns.

Enraged by this deception, Zeus intensified Prometheus’s punishment, sending an eagle to devour his ever-regenerating liver daily. Nevertheless, through cunning, foresight, and sacrifice, Prometheus secured humanity’s ascendance—granting mortals not merely survival, but enduring dominion over the terrestrial realm.

title: A Machine Learning Model for Accurate Prediction of Sepsis in ICU Patients
human: Background: Although numerous studies are conducted every year on how to reduce the fatality rate associated with sepsis, it is still a major challenge faced by patients, clinicians, and medical systems worldwide. Early identification and prediction of patients at risk of sepsis and adverse outcomes associated with sepsis are critical. We aimed to develop an artificial intelligence algorithm that can predict sepsis early. Methods: This was a secondary analysis of an observational cohort study from the Intensive Care Unit of the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University. A total of 4,449 infected patients were randomly assigned to the development and validation data set at a ratio of 4:1. After extracting electronic medical record data, a set of 55 features (variables) was calculated and passed to the random forest algorithm to predict the onset of sepsis. Results: The pre-procedure clinical variables were used to build a prediction model from the training data set using the random forest machine learning method; a 5-fold cross-validation was used to evaluate the prediction accuracy of the model. Finally, we tested the model using the validation data set. The area obtained by the model under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) was 0.91, the sensitivity was 87%, and the specificity was 89%. Conclusions: This newly established machine learning-based model has shown good predictive ability in Chinese sepsis patients. External validation studies are necessary to confirm the universality of our method in the population and treatment practice.
text:
Background: Despite extensive annual research aimed at reducing sepsis-related mortality, sepsis remains a formidable global challenge for patients, clinicians, and healthcare systems alike. Early identification of individuals at risk for sepsis—and for adverse sepsis-related outcomes—is therefore critical. In this study, we developed an artificial intelligence–based algorithm to enable early prediction of sepsis.  

Methods: We performed a secondary analysis of an observational cohort study conducted in the intensive care unit (ICU) of the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University. A total of 4,449 infected patients were randomly allocated to development and validation datasets in a 4:1 ratio. From electronic health records, we extracted and computed 55 clinical features, which served as inputs to a random forest algorithm designed to predict sepsis onset.  

Results: Using pre-procedural clinical variables from the training dataset, we trained a random forest model; its performance was assessed via five-fold cross-validation. The final model was then evaluated on the independent validation dataset. It achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.91, with sensitivity and specificity of 87% and 89%, respectively.  

Conclusions: This newly developed machine learning model demonstrates strong predictive performance for sepsis in a Chinese patient population. External validation in diverse clinical settings is warranted to assess its generalizability across populations and real-world practice.

title: Mechanisms of elevated CO2-induced thermotolerance in plants: the role of phytohormones
human: Rising atmospheric CO2 is a key driver of climate change, intensifying drastic changes in meteorological parameters. Plants can sense and respond to changes in environmental parameters including atmospheric CO2 and temperatures. High temperatures beyond the physiological threshold can significantly affect plant growth and development and thus attenuate crop productivity. However, elevated atmospheric CO2 can mitigate the deleterious effects of heat stress on plants. Despite a large body of literature supporting the positive impact of elevated CO2 on thermotolerance, the underlying biological mechanisms and precise molecular pathways that lead to enhanced tolerance to heat stress remain largely unclear. Under heat stress, elevated CO2-induced expression of respiratory burst oxidase homologs (RBOHs) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling play a critical role in stomatal movement, which optimizes gas exchange to enhance photosynthesis and water use efficiency. Notably, elevated CO2 also fortifies antioxidant defense and redox homeostasis to alleviate heat-induced oxidative damage. Both hormone-dependent and independent pathways have been shown to mediate high CO2-induced thermotolerance. The activation of heat-shock factors and subsequent expression of heat-shock proteins are thought to be the essential mechanism downstream of hormone and ROS signaling. Here we review the role of phytohormones in plant response to high atmospheric CO2 and temperatures. We also discuss the potential mechanisms of elevated CO2-induced thermotolerance by focusing on several key phytohormones such as ethylene. Finally, we address some limitations of our current understanding and the need for further research to unveil the yet-unknown crosstalk between plant hormones in mediating high CO2-induced thermotolerance in plants.

title: A survey of values and related factors among 200 guardians of children with epilepsy
human: Epilepsy is a common disease in the pediatric neurology department; as it a chronic disease, many years are spent seeing doctors and taking drugs. The objective of the study is to understand the values of parents to help doctors to more effectively communicate and to improve patient compliance. The study was designed to investigate guardians' values of children with epilepsy and analyze the relevant factors that may affect these values and the correlation of the guardians' values and medical decision making. Two hundred guardians (93 men and 107 women) of children with epilepsy from three hospitals in Wuhan, China, were selected at random and investigated by means of interview survey. Statistical analysis by ratio was conducted on the general data, whereas statistical analyses by Pearson and Spearman rank correlation were conducted for the relative factors. A high educational level among male guardians indicated a strong tendency to read up on epilepsy, which influenced their care given. A high educational level among female guardians indicated better capability to take care of child patients and follow directions for antiepileptic drug administration. Female guardians were more likely to see the same doctors during a long disease period than male guardians. The guardians' values were influenced by many factors, such as gender, education, and duration of disease. Guardians' values need to be considered as they are helpful for doctors in decision-making.
text: Epilepsy is a common condition in pediatric neurology; as a chronic disorder, it often requires years of medical follow-up and long-term antiepileptic drug therapy. This study aimed to identify the values held by parents of children with epilepsy—to support more effective clinician–parent communication and improve treatment adherence. Specifically, it investigated guardians’ values, analyzed factors associated with those values, and examined how those values relate to medical decision-making. A total of 200 guardians (93 fathers and 107 mothers) of children with epilepsy were randomly recruited from three hospitals in Wuhan, China, and interviewed using a structured survey. Descriptive statistics summarized demographic data, while Pearson and Spearman rank correlation analyses assessed relationships between guardians’ values and potential influencing factors. Higher educational attainment among fathers was associated with greater engagement in epilepsy-related information-seeking, which shaped their caregiving approach. Among mothers, higher education correlated with stronger capacity to manage their child’s care and adhere to antiepileptic medication regimens. Mothers were also significantly more likely than fathers to maintain continuity of care with the same physician over the course of the illness. Guardians’ values were influenced by multiple factors—including gender, education level, and disease duration—and should be explicitly considered in clinical decision-making to enhance shared understanding and collaborative care.

title: Turfgrass intercropping prevents non-point source pollution in sweet pepper production
human: Greenhouse vegetable production is one of the major non-point source (NPS) pollution due to its high fertilizer input and low nutrient use efficiency. Excessive salt and nutrient accumulation in the topsoil is responsible for the NPS pollution in greenhouse vegetable production. This study was designed to investigate the effects of turfgrass intercropping on NPS pollution in greenhouse sweet pepper production. The results showed that the pollution discharges via both surface runoff and leaching were significantly reduced by turfgrass intercropping. The reduction of pollution was associated with the capacity of turfgrass species in the absorption and accumulation of salts and nitrate. Paspalum vaginatum with preferential accumulations of nitrate and salts performed best results in the alleviation of soil salinity and NPS pollution. Paspalum vaginatum-intercropping decreased 51.2% of nitrate and 23.9% of electrical conductivity in the soil, 71.8% of total nitrogen, 54.9% of ammonia-nitrogen, 67.0% of nitrate-nitrogen, 68.8% of total phosphorus, 68.2% of phosphates, and 73.2% of potassium in the surface runoff, and 64.1% of total nitrogen, 53.4% of ammonia-nitrogen, 67.0% of nitrate-nitrogen, 44.3% of total phosphorus, 54.8% of phosphates, and 32.9% of potassium in the leachate. These results indicated that Paspalum vaginatum-intercropping could be a clean and sustainable solution to prevent NPS pollution in greenhouse vegetable production.
text: Greenhouse vegetable production is a significant contributor to non-point source (NPS) pollution, primarily due to high fertilizer inputs and low nutrient use efficiency. This inefficiency leads to excessive accumulation of salts and nutrients—particularly nitrogen and phosphorus—in the topsoil, which subsequently leach or run off into surrounding environments. To address this challenge, this study evaluated the potential of turfgrass intercropping to mitigate NPS pollution in greenhouse-grown sweet pepper systems. Results demonstrated that intercropping with turfgrass significantly reduced pollutant losses via both surface runoff and leachate. The mitigation effect was attributed to the turfgrass species’ capacity to absorb and accumulate excess salts and nitrate from the soil–water system. Among the species tested, *Paspalum vaginatum*—which exhibited a strong preference for accumulating nitrate and soluble salts—proved most effective in alleviating soil salinity and reducing NPS pollution. Specifically, *P. vaginatum* intercropping decreased soil nitrate concentration by 51.2% and electrical conductivity (a proxy for salinity) by 23.9%. In surface runoff, it reduced total nitrogen (71.8%), ammonia-nitrogen (54.9%), nitrate-nitrogen (67.0%), total phosphorus (68.8%), phosphate (68.2%), and potassium (73.2%). In leachate, corresponding reductions were 64.1% (total nitrogen), 53.4% (ammonia-nitrogen), 67.0% (nitrate-nitrogen), 44.3% (total phosphorus), 54.8% (phosphate), and 32.9% (potassium). Collectively, these findings indicate that intercropping with *Paspalum vaginatum* offers a clean, practical, and sustainable strategy for controlling NPS pollution in intensive greenhouse vegetable production systems.

text:
For months, hundreds of aspiring contract workers have been stranded in a dilapidated warehouse at Baghdad International Airport—sleeping four to a bed, subsisting on inadequate food, and without funds. They say they were deceived by unscrupulous recruitment agents into traveling to Iraq for jobs that never existed.

The men, currently housed in the airport warehouse, paid recruiters substantial fees—between $3,000 and $5,000—to arrange their travel to Iraq, believing they would be employed by American defense contractor KBR through a Kuwaiti firm, Najlaa Catering Services. Recruiters targeted workers from India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Uganda, promising them secure positions. Many sold farms or other assets to raise the required sums.

Upon arrival in Baghdad, however, they found themselves confined—with approximately 1,000 others—in a compound inside the airport perimeter, guarded by private security personnel. About 600 were crammed into a single-room warehouse. Though showers are present, the taps are nonfunctional and unusable.

Many remain uncertain about the validity of their visas and their legal status in Iraq. Legally barred from staying and financially unable to return home, they are effectively trapped. When asked whether their home governments had offered assistance, they replied uniformly: “Nothing, nothing.”

Protests have drawn harsh responses: several men reported that guards fired warning shots into the air to silence them. (Watch footage of the men in the warehouse »)

Najlaa’s representatives in Iraq declined to comment when approached by CNN. Its Kuwaiti office described the situation as “under control” and stated it was being addressed.

Some Ugandan nationals alleged that Iraqi police detained and physically abused them. One recounted being told: “If you’re here for the U.S., we’ll show you the difference between the U.S. government and the Iraqi government—let’s see if the U.S. will help you.” Iraqi authorities declined to respond to these allegations.

As the men spoke with CNN on camera, an official overseeing them threatened to lock them out of the compound unless they returned indoors within two minutes.

KBR confirmed it played no role in recruiting these individuals. In a statement to CNN, the company emphasized that it does not condone unethical conduct and requires its contractors to adhere strictly to its Code of Conduct—including mandatory training on human trafficking prevention. KBR added that, upon learning of potential trafficking cases, it works “to remediate the problem and report the matter to the appropriate authorities,” and collaborates with those authorities to resolve the issue.

Meanwhile, at a separate, makeshift camp nearby, another group of men said they were similarly misled—by different recruiters—and now rely on food donations from Iraqi workers. Their recruiters have vanished. These men, too, face immigration limbo: many have had their passports confiscated—or visa pages torn out.

Assistance may be forthcoming. The men said United Nations staff had visited them. The UN confirmed to CNN that it is aware of the situation and is assessing how best to support those affected. The U.S. military told CNN it takes allegations of human rights abuses seriously and is investigating the matter. Iraqi authorities have also seized the passport of a Najlaa official pending resolution of the crisis.

Yet for the stranded men, time is running out. “It’s not fair,” one said.

This report was contributed to by CNN’s Thomas Evans and Jomana Karadsheh.

title: Agronomic Biofortification of Cayenne Pepper Cultivars with Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria and Chili Residue in a Chinese Solar Greenhouse
human: Agronomic biofortification of horticultural crops using plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) under crop residue incorporation systems remains largely underexploited. Bacillus subtilis (B1), Bacillus laterosporus (B2), or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (B3) was inoculated on soil containing chili residue, while chili residue without PGPR (NP) served as the control. Two hybrid long cayenne peppers, succeeding a leaf mustard crop were used in the intensive cultivation study. Net photosynthesis, leaf stomatal conductance, transpiration rate, photosynthetic water use efficiency, shoot and root biomass, and fruit yield were evaluated. Derivatives of folate, minerals, and nitrate contents in the pepper fruits were also assessed. B1 elicited higher net photosynthesis and photosynthetic water use efficiency, while B2 and B3 had higher transpiration rates than B1 and NP. B1 and B3 resulted in 27-36% increase in pepper fruit yield compared to other treatments, whereas B3 produced 24-27.5% and 21.9-27.2% higher 5-methyltetrahydrofolate and total folate contents, respectively, compared to B1 and NP. However, chili residue without PGPR inoculation improved fruit calcium, magnesium, and potassium contents than the inoculated treatments. 'Xin Xian La 8 F1' cultivar had higher yield and plant biomass, fruit potassium, total soluble solids, and total folate contents compared to 'La Gao F1.' Agronomic biofortification through the synergy of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens and chili residue produced better yield and folate contents with a trade-off in the mineral contents of the greenhouse-grown long cayenne pepper.

title: The complete chloroplast genome sequence of Vitis vinifera × Vitis labrusca 'Shenhua'
human: Vitis vinifera × Vitis labrusca 'Shenhua' is a tetraploid grape, a Franco-american species. This study first published the complete chloroplast genome of Vitis vinifera × Vitis labrusca 'Shenhua' was assembled. The chloroplast genome is 160928 bp in length, including a large single copy region (89,148 bp), a small single-copy region (19,072 bp) and a pair of inverted repeats of 26,354 bp. The chloroplast genome encodes 133 genes, comprising 88 CDSs, 37 tRNA genes and 8 rRNA genes. The phylogenetic tree demonstrated that Vitis vinifera × Vitis labrusca 'Shenhua' is different from the other 16 varieties.
text: Vitis vinifera × Vitis labrusca ‘Shenhua’ is a tetraploid, Franco-American grape cultivar. This study reports the first complete assembly and characterization of its chloroplast genome. The genome is 160,928 bp long and comprises a large single-copy region (89,148 bp), a small single-copy region (19,072 bp), and a pair of inverted repeats (26,354 bp each). It encodes 133 genes: 88 protein-coding sequences (CDSs), 37 tRNA genes, and 8 rRNA genes. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that ‘Shenhua’ forms a distinct clade, clearly differentiated from the other 16 grape varieties examined.

title: Thymic T-Cell Production Is Associated With Changes in the Gut Microbiota in Young Chicks
human: Increasing studies show that gut microbiota play a central role in immunity, although the impact of the microbiota on mediation of thymic T cells throughout life is not well understood. Chickens have been shown to be a valuable model for studying basic immunology. Here, we show that changes in the gut microbiota are associated with the development of thymic T cells in young chickens. Our results showed that T-cell numbers in newborn chicks sharply increased from day 0 and peaked at day 49. Interestingly, the α-diversity score pattern of change in gut microbiota also increased after day 0 and continued to increase until day 49. We found that early antibiotic treatment resulted in a dramatic reduction in gut alpha diversity: principal component analysis (PCA) showed that antibiotic treatment resulted in a different cluster from the controls on days 9 and 49. In the antibiotic-treated chickens, we identified eight significantly different (p < 0.05) microbes at the phylum level and 14 significantly different (p < 0.05) microbes at the genus level, compared with the controls. Importantly, we found that antibiotic treatment led to a decreased percentage and number of T cells in the thymus when measured at days 9 and 49, as evaluated by flow cytometry. Collectively, our data suggest that intestinal microbiota may be involved in the regulation of T cells in birds, presenting the possibility that interventions that actively modify the gut microbiota in early life may accelerate the maturation of humoral immunity, with resulting anti-inflammatory effects against different pathogens.
text: Emerging evidence underscores the pivotal role of the gut microbiota in modulating immune function. However, the influence of the microbiota on thymic T-cell development across the lifespan remains poorly characterized. Chickens serve as a well-established and physiologically relevant model for fundamental immunological research. In this study, we demonstrate a temporal association between gut microbial community dynamics and thymic T-cell development in young chickens. Specifically, thymic T-cell numbers increased sharply from day 0 post-hatch and reached a peak at day 49. Notably, gut microbial α-diversity followed a parallel trajectory—rising after day 0 and continuing to increase through day 49. Early-life antibiotic treatment markedly reduced α-diversity, with principal component analysis (PCA) revealing distinct clustering of antibiotic-treated birds relative to controls at both day 9 and day 49. At the taxonomic level, antibiotic exposure significantly altered microbial composition: eight phyla and fourteen genera differed significantly (p < 0.05) between treated and control groups. Crucially, flow cytometric analysis revealed that antibiotic treatment significantly reduced both the proportion and absolute number of thymic T cells at days 9 and 49. Together, these findings indicate that the intestinal microbiota contributes to the regulation of thymic T-cell development in avian species. This suggests that targeted early-life modulation of the gut microbiota may promote accelerated maturation of humoral immunity and confer broad-spectrum anti-inflammatory protection against diverse pathogens.

title: Radiomics and Machine Learning With Multiparametric Preoperative MRI May Accurately Predict the Histopathological Grades of Soft Tissue Sarcomas
human: Preoperative prediction of the grade of soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) is important because of its effect on treatment planning. To assess the value of radiomics features in distinguishing histological grades of STSs. Retrospective. In all, 113 patients with pathology-confirmed low-grade (grade I), intermediate-grade (grade II), or high-grade (grade III) soft tissue sarcoma were collected. The 3.0T axial T1 -weighted imaging (T1 WI) with 550 msec repetition time (TR); 18 msec echo time (TE), 312 × 312 matrix, fat-suppressed fast spin-echo T2 WI with 4291 msec TR, 85 msec TE, 312 × 312 matrix. Multiple machine-learning methods were trained to establish classification models for predicting STS grades. Eighty STS patients (18 low-grade [grade I]; 62 high-grade [grades II-III]) were enrolled in the primary set and we tested the model with a validation set with 33 patients (7 low-grade, 26 high-grade). 1) Student's t-tests were applied for continuous variables and the χ2 test were applied for categorical variables between low-grade STS and high-grade STS groups. 2) For feature subset selection, either no subset selection or recursive feature elimination was performed. This technology was combined with random forest and support vector machine-learning methods. Finally, to overcome the disparity in the frequencies of the STS grades, each machine-learning model was trained i) without subsampling, ii) with the synthetic minority oversampling technique, and iii) with random oversampling examples, for a total of 12 combinations of machine-learning algorithms that were assessed, trained, and tested in the validation cohort. The best classification model for the prediction of STS grade was a combination of features selected by recursive feature elimination and random forest classification algorithms with a synthetic minority oversampling technique, which had an area under the curve of 0.9615 (95% confidence interval 0.8944-1.0) in the validation set. Radiomics feature-based machine-learning methods are useful for distinguishing STS grades. 3 Technical Efficacy: Stage 2 J. Magn. Reson. Imaging 2020;51:791-797.
text:
Preoperative prediction of soft tissue sarcoma (STS) grade is clinically important, as it directly influences treatment planning. This study evaluated the utility of radiomics features derived from routine MRI for distinguishing histological grades of STS. A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from 113 patients with pathologically confirmed STS—comprising 18 low-grade (grade I), 62 intermediate- or high-grade (grades II–III) tumors. Imaging included axial T1-weighted images (3.0T; TR = 550 ms, TE = 18 ms, matrix = 312 × 312) and fat-suppressed fast spin-echo T2-weighted images (TR = 4291 ms, TE = 85 ms, matrix = 312 × 312).  

Machine learning models—including random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM)—were trained to classify STS grade. The cohort was divided into a primary training set (n = 80: 18 low-grade, 62 high-grade [grades II–III]) and an independent validation set (n = 33: 7 low-grade, 26 high-grade). Statistical comparisons between low- and high-grade groups employed Student’s *t*-tests for continuous variables and χ² tests for categorical variables. For feature selection, we evaluated both no selection and recursive feature elimination (RFE). To address class imbalance, each model was trained under three resampling strategies: (i) no subsampling, (ii) synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE), and (iii) random oversampling—yielding a total of 12 distinct algorithm–selection–resampling combinations. All models were trained and validated on the same split.  

The optimal model combined RFE-selected radiomics features with RF classification and SMOTE resampling, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9615 (95% CI: 0.8944–1.0) in the validation set. These findings demonstrate that radiomics-based machine learning holds promise for noninvasive preoperative grading of STS.  
*Technical Efficacy: Stage 2*  
*J Magn Reson Imaging.* 2020;51:791–797.

title: Evolutionary and expression analysis of CAMTA gene family in Nicotiana tabacum yielded insights into their origin, expansion and stress responses
human: Calmodulin-binding transcription activators (CAMTAs) represent the novel gene family of transcriptional regulators, which play important biological functions. Though, the first ever plant CAMTA gene was evidenced in Nicotiana tabacum in 2002. But, the systematic identification, origin and function of this gene family has not been performed due to the lack of reference genome information until now. Here, we identified 29 CAMTA genes in four Nicotiana species, including thirteen NtabCAMTAs, six NsylCAMTAs, and five NtomCAMTAs and NbenCAMTAs. These CAMTA families were classified into five phylogenetic groups (I-V), among which, the group-IV CAMTAs probably emerged the earliest. The NtabCAMTA family genes have diverse structures, and are randomly localized on five chromosomes and scaffolds. N. tabacum acquired 11 copies of homolog CAMATA genes from the parental genomes of N. tomentosiformis and N. sylvestris, followed by expansion through polyploidization and duplication. The NtabCAMTA genes were differentially expressed in different plant parts, and showed sensitivity towards different abiotic and biotic stresses. Co-expression network analysis revealed that some NtabCAMTA subunits interact with each other, and co-expressed. The current study is the first report presenting a comprehensive overview of Nicotiana CAMTA families, and opens a new avenue for the improvement of the cultivated tobacco.

title: Research on the formation of humanistic care ability in nursing students: A structural equation approach
human: To construct and test a hypothetical model linking the caring ability of nursing students with empathy ability, emotional intelligence, and communication ability. Participants were 851 students from three undergraduate colleges and one junior college in China, Gansu Province. Participating students had to fulfill the following requirements: different levels of nursing majors (undergraduates or junior college students), understand the study purpose, and be willing to participate in this study. Exclusion: secondary college students. Variables were measured by the Caring Ability Inventory, Emotional Intelligence Scale, Supportive Communicative Scale, and Interpersonal Reactivity Index. Data were analyzed with structural equation modeling to explore the path relationships and mutual effects between structural elements. Empathy (β = 0.25, P<0.001), emotional intelligence (β = 0.36, P<0.001), and communication ability (β = 0.28, P<0.001) were significantly associated with the caring ability of nursing students. Empathy was the strongest factor associated with caring ability and emotional intelligence was a partial mediator of the relationship between empathy and communication skills. The nurse's humanistic care ability requires continuous learning and school education. To enhance the humanistic care ability of nursing students, nursing educators should develop target strategies to improve the 'sympathetic ability,' 'emotional intelligence' and 'communication ability' of nursing students.
text: This study aimed to develop and test a hypothetical model linking nursing students’ caring ability with their empathy, emotional intelligence, and communication ability. Participants included 851 undergraduate and junior college nursing students from three universities and one vocational college in Gansu Province, China. Eligible students were enrolled in nursing programs at either the undergraduate or junior college level, understood the study’s purpose, and provided informed consent. Students from secondary vocational colleges were excluded. Caring ability was assessed using the Caring Ability Inventory; empathy, with the Interpersonal Reactivity Index; emotional intelligence, with the Emotional Intelligence Scale; and communication ability, with the Supportive Communicative Scale. Structural equation modeling was used to examine direct and indirect pathways among these constructs. Results indicated that empathy (β = 0.25, *p* < 0.001), emotional intelligence (β = 0.36, *p* < 0.001), and communication ability (β = 0.28, *p* < 0.001) all significantly predicted caring ability—with emotional intelligence emerging as the strongest predictor. Moreover, emotional intelligence partially mediated the relationship between empathy and communication ability. Cultivating humanistic caring competence requires sustained learning and robust academic support. To strengthen this capacity, nursing educators should implement targeted interventions designed to enhance students’ empathy, emotional intelligence, and communication skills.

title: Heavy metal contamination of agricultural soils affected by mining activities around the Ganxi River in Chenzhou, Southern China
human: Heavy metal contamination attracted a wide spread attention due to their strong toxicity and persistence. The Ganxi River, located in Chenzhou City, Southern China, has been severely polluted by lead/zinc ore mining activities. This work investigated the heavy metal pollution in agricultural soils around the Ganxi River. The total concentrations of heavy metals were determined by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry. The potential risk associated with the heavy metals in soil was assessed by Nemerow comprehensive index and potential ecological risk index. In both methods, the study area was rated as very high risk. Multivariate statistical methods including Pearson's correlation analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and principal component analysis were employed to evaluate the relationships between heavy metals, as well as the correlation between heavy metals and pH, to identify the metal sources. Three distinct clusters have been observed by hierarchical cluster analysis. In principal component analysis, a total of two components were extracted to explain over 90% of the total variance, both of which were associated with anthropogenic sources.
text: Heavy metal contamination has drawn widespread scientific and regulatory attention due to its high toxicity and environmental persistence. The Ganxi River—located in Chenzhou City, southern China—has suffered severe pollution as a result of long-standing lead–zinc ore mining activities. This study assessed heavy metal contamination in agricultural soils surrounding the river. Total concentrations of heavy metals were quantified using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Ecological and health risks were evaluated using two widely accepted indices: the Nemerow comprehensive pollution index and the potential ecological risk index (PERI). Both assessments classified the study area as posing a *very high* risk. To elucidate the sources and interrelationships among heavy metals—and their association with soil pH—multivariate statistical techniques were applied, including Pearson’s correlation analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), and principal component analysis (PCA). HCA revealed three distinct metal groupings, while PCA identified two principal components accounting for over 90% of the total variance—both strongly linked to anthropogenic (mining-related) sources.

title: Using E-GARCH to Analyze the Impact of Investor Sentiment on Stock Returns Near Stock Market Crashes
human: Purpose: Investor sentiment, the willingness of market participants to invest, is a difficult concept to measure. Exploring the relationship between investor sentiment and stock returns can reveal how investor sentiment affects the operation of the stock market. Such an understanding can assist market participants in making more rational investment decisions based on market laws. Such an understanding can also assist regulators in their roles of supervision and policy making. Methodology: Although the E-GARCH model has the advantage of considering volatility clustering, it has not previously been used to investigate the impact of investor sentiment changes on the Shanghai Composite Index's market return. This research therefore applies the E-GARCH approach to data from 2015 to 2018, to explore the influence of investor sentiment on the return rate of the Shanghai Composite Index. Main Findings: There are three main findings. First, when the investor sentiment is increased by the same amount, the rate of return before a stock market crash will have a smaller increase than the rate of change after the crash, which is a new finding. Second, the rate of return on stocks is susceptible to emotional sentiment, rather than simply depending on stock price. Third, the tendency of retail investors to follow the crowd is less in periods of pessimism than it is in periods of optimism, which, in turn, can push up stock yields. Application: Based on these research results, this article can provide insights to understand how investors' subjective judgments on future earnings affect their investment behavior and how great the impact is on the market. At the same time, it can help investors make more rational investment decisions based on an understanding of market laws, and help regulators with guidance for their supervision and policy making. Originality/Value: This paper contributes to the theory of the investor sentiment index, improving the index construction method by adding two sentiment proxy indicators: investor activity ACT and stock market leverage level. After constructing the sentiment index and comparing it with the stock market index (Shanghai Composite Index), the fit is found to be improved.
text:
Purpose:  
Investor sentiment—the willingness of market participants to invest—is inherently difficult to quantify. Investigating its relationship with stock returns can shed light on how sentiment shapes the functioning of equity markets. Such insights help investors make more rational, evidence-based decisions aligned with underlying market dynamics—and equip regulators with a stronger empirical foundation for supervision and policy formulation.  

Methodology:  
While the E-GARCH model effectively captures volatility clustering, it has not yet been applied to examine how shifts in investor sentiment influence returns on the Shanghai Composite Index (SCI). To address this gap, we employ the E-GARCH framework to analyze daily data from 2015 to 2018, specifically assessing the impact of investor sentiment on SCI returns.  

Main Findings:  
Our analysis yields three key insights. First, a given increase in investor sentiment leads to a smaller rise in returns *before* a market crash than *after*—a novel finding that highlights asymmetry in sentiment’s effect across market regimes. Second, stock returns are significantly influenced by investor sentiment—not merely by price levels or fundamentals alone. Third, retail investors’ herding behavior is weaker during periods of pessimism than during optimism—a dynamic that, counterintuitively, contributes to higher subsequent stock returns.  

Practical Implications:  
These findings deepen our understanding of how investors’ subjective expectations about future earnings shape their behavior—and how profoundly such expectations influence market outcomes. For practitioners, the results support more disciplined, sentiment-aware investment strategies grounded in market regularities. For policymakers, they offer actionable intelligence to refine regulatory oversight and design more effective macroprudential measures.  

Originality/Value:  
This study advances the literature on investor sentiment indices by enhancing index construction: we incorporate two new sentiment proxies—investor activity (ACT) and stock market leverage—into an improved sentiment index. When benchmarked against the Shanghai Composite Index, the revised index demonstrates markedly better fit and explanatory power.

“Employment-at-will” Doctrine Essay

“Employment-at-will” (EAW) legislation provides regulations and rules that govern private employment. Its provisions ensure minimal regulation of employment practices such as termination and dismissal of employees. According to the doctrine, an employer may terminate an employee without a proper explanation or reason.

On the other hand, an employee may quit a job at any time without being liable to the employer for inconvenience. Approximately 55% of employees in the private sector in the United States are under the jurisdiction legislation. The principle of the legislation has come under attack in the recent past for its alleged unethical nature. Despite the attack, some people see its ethical nature and fully support it.

Opponents of the doctrine present several claims for rejecting it. First, it does not provide and protect the rights of employees from the perspective of moral rights. For example, it does not stipulate clearly the political, democratic and privacy rights of employees. Therefore, employers can violate employees’ rights without being held liable.

It is discriminatory because employers and employees do not have equal rights. For example, they should all have equal rights to speech. Moreover, it denies employees rights to work-contributions even though managers have rights to execute property claims. However, proponents of the doctrine argue that such legislation does not extend to the private sector and is therefore valid. Employers and employee sign work contracts.

Therefore, workers should set their terms during negotiation stage on how they wish to be treated. Secondly, the EAW does not promote fairness in employer/employee relationship. EAW requires both parties to treat each other fairly and equally. However, implementation of EAW yields different results. It is weak, unreliable, and insufficient. Employers practice power and control over employees because EAW allows them.

It encourages inconsistent and irrational management behavior that results in mistreatment of employees by employers. In addition, it promotes errant behaviors by employees such as quitting their jobs without giving notice to employers. The doctrine is not fair to employees because it promotes harshness and contains assumptions that compromise the employer/employee relationship in favor of employers.

Proponents argue that EAW promotes good practices such as recognition of performing employees by employers. This encourages a “people first’ approach to organizational matters that benefits both employees and employers. Employees are treated with respect. It encourages fair labor practices such as guaranteeing employment security, fir remuneration, and employee empowerment.

In addition, public policy exceptions contained in the doctrine protect the rights of employees and prevents unfair dismissal or termination. Employees may lodge claims against their employers if treated unfairly in contradiction to policy exceptions of the doctrine. Therefore, it protects the rights of employees and prevents employers from terminating employees without good reasons. The “at will” doctrine is flexible in that it can be altered by contract.

For example, an employer and employee can agree that termination can only result from violation of certain agreed conditions. Therefore, dismissing the doctrine as weak and inefficient is erroneous. Another argument in support of the doctrine is that it promotes flexibility and does not hold any party liable for any decision made. It allows an employee to leave if he/she is unsatisfied with the employer. This prevents violation of employees’ rights.

On the other hand, the employer can terminate an employee at will on grounds of poor performance without any liability. Proponents also argue that the doctrine promotes professionalism because the employee can control her career without the interference of the employer. title: Building a profile of subjective well-being for social media users
human: Subjective well-being includes 'affect' and 'satisfaction with life' (SWL). This study proposes a unified approach to construct a profile of subjective well-being based on social media language in Facebook status updates. We apply sentiment analysis to generate users' affect scores, and train a random forest model to predict SWL using affect scores and other language features of the status updates. Results show that: the computer-selected features resemble the key predictors of SWL as identified in early studies; the machine-predicted SWL is moderately correlated with the self-reported SWL (r = 0.36, p < 0.01), indicating that language-based assessment can constitute valid SWL measures; the machine-assessed affect scores resemble those reported in a previous experimental study; and the machine-predicted subjective well-being profile can also reflect other psychological traits like depression (r = 0.24, p < 0.01). This study provides important insights for psychological prediction using multiple, machine-assessed components and longitudinal or dense psychological assessment using social media language.
text: Subjective well-being (SWB) comprises two core dimensions: affect and life satisfaction (LS). This study introduces a unified framework for constructing SWB profiles from Facebook status updates using natural language. We derive users’ affect scores via sentiment analysis and train a random forest model to predict LS using these affect scores alongside other linguistic features. Key findings include: (1) the model’s top-selected features align closely with established psychological predictors of LS; (2) machine-predicted LS shows a moderate, statistically significant correlation with self-reported LS (r = 0.36, p < 0.01), supporting the validity of language-based LS assessment; (3) the automated affect scores closely mirror those observed in prior experimental work; and (4) the overall machine-generated SWB profile correlates significantly with depression symptoms (r = 0.24, p < 0.01). These results advance psychological assessment by demonstrating how multi-component, machine-derived SWB metrics—derived longitudinally or densely from social media language—can yield meaningful, empirically grounded insights.

text:
Budget Travel’s Top Five Travel Booking Sites  

After conducting thousands of searches annually, the editors of *Budget Travel* have identified five online resources that consistently deliver exceptional value for booking flights, hotels, and other travel essentials. Here’s why each stands out:  

Dohop.com  
Specializing exclusively in international airfare—*outside the U.S.*—Dohop excels at finding low-cost options between cities like Paris and Rome. Its powerful search engine simultaneously scans multiple airports serving the same metropolitan area (e.g., all five London airports) and pulls fares from budget carriers such as EasyJet and Ryanair—many of which larger travel platforms overlook. Note, however, that Dohop is significantly less effective for flights originating in the United States.  

Kayak.com  
Widely regarded as the most reliable site for securing the lowest domestic airfares in the U.S., Kayak distinguishes itself through seamless usability. Unlike many competitors—which redirect users to external pages where critical details (like departure times) may only appear *after* clicking, or worse, require re-entering search criteria—Kayak sends you directly to the airline’s website with the exact fare and flight you selected, guaranteed. For travelers with flexible schedules, Kayak’s flexible-date search tool offers the broadest coverage of routes and airports among all sites we’ve tested.  

Priceline.com  
A pioneer in discount travel, Priceline helps airlines, hotels, and car-rental companies move unsold inventory at deeply discounted rates. While its “Name Your Own Price” feature—where travelers bid without knowing specific details until after acceptance—may not suit everyone, it remains a powerful tool for flexible travelers. Bidding for upscale hotels in major cities often yields savings of up to 50% compared to standard rates. The trade-off is uncertainty about the exact location—but in vibrant urban destinations where sightseeing takes you across neighborhoods, this is rarely a drawback. Priceline also offers traditional, transparent bookings, though in our assessment, its performance in this mode is on par with Expedia, Travelocity, Orbitz, and CheapTickets—not superior.  

TripAdvisor.com  
As the leading platform for user-generated hotel reviews, TripAdvisor leverages collective traveler experience to help users make informed decisions. While the mix of positive, negative, and mixed reviews for a single property can be overwhelming, reading critically—filtering out outliers or biased entries—provides genuine insight into what to expect. Though newer entrants like TravelPost (a Kayak-owned site offering similar functionality) are emerging, TripAdvisor remains unmatched in both volume and depth of reviews. To date, TravelPost hosts only about one-tenth as many opinions as TripAdvisor.  

Venere.com  
Venere specializes in independently owned accommodations across Europe and beyond—properties often absent from mainstream U.S.-based booking platforms. While most sites highlight large, internationally recognized hotels, Venere shines when you’re seeking character-rich alternatives: family-run inns, boutique guesthouses, apartments, pensions, or even rural farmhouses. These options frequently deliver superior value. For example, a recent search for Nice, France, yielded 20 Venere-listed properties charging under €60 ($82) per night—well below typical resort-town rates for chain hotels.

title: Genetic parameters of seven immune factors in turbot (Scophthalmus maximus) infected with Vibrio anguillarum
human: In this study, 1,800 turbot (Scophthalmus maximus) individuals from 30 full-sib families were experimentally infected with Vibrio anguillarum, and the expression levels of the immune factors lysozyme, hepcidin, heat-shock protein 70 (HSP70), HSP90, immunoglobulin M (IgM), C-type lectin and Lily-type lectin in the liver were measured by real-time PCR. Heritability values of the seven immune factors were 0.289 ± 0.087, 0.092 ± 0.024, 0.282 ± 0.043, 0.244 ± 0.027, 0.343 ± 0.081, 0.092 ± 0.011 and 0.084 ± 0.009, respectively. The ranges of phenotypic, genetic and environmental correlations were -0.889 to 0.759, -0.841 to 0.888 and -0.919 to 0.883, respectively. The heritability values of HSP70, HSP90 and IgM were moderate, and the genetic correlations between HSP70, HSP90 and IgM were moderate to highly positive, which suggests that the immunocompetence of turbot against V. anguillarum can be improved by genetically improving these three immune characters via multi-trait integrated breeding technology or indirect selection.
text: In this study, 1,800 turbot (*Scophthalmus maximus*) individuals from 30 full-sib families were experimentally challenged with *Vibrio anguillarum*. Using quantitative real-time PCR, we measured hepatic expression levels of seven immune-related genes: lysozyme, hepcidin, heat-shock protein 70 (HSP70), HSP90, immunoglobulin M (IgM), C-type lectin, and L-type lectin. Estimated heritabilities for these traits were 0.289 ± 0.087, 0.092 ± 0.024, 0.282 ± 0.043, 0.244 ± 0.027, 0.343 ± 0.081, 0.092 ± 0.011, and 0.084 ± 0.009, respectively. Phenotypic, genetic, and environmental correlations among the traits ranged from −0.889 to 0.759, −0.841 to 0.888, and −0.919 to 0.883, respectively. Notably, HSP70, HSP90, and IgM exhibited moderate heritability and showed moderate-to-strong positive genetic correlations—indicating that selective breeding targeting these three traits—either directly or indirectly via multi-trait selection strategies—could effectively enhance turbot resistance to *V. anguillarum*.

title: Awareness, knowledge and attitudes towards cardiopulmonary resuscitation among people with and without heart disease relatives in South China: a cross-sectional survey
human: To assess the awareness, knowledge and attitudes towards cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) among relatives of people with and without heart disease and their influence in South China. This is a cross-sectional survey. Logistic regression was used to evaluate the demographic factors associated with CPR training, learning and knowledge. The study was conducted in two hospitals, the largest cardiovascular institute and the largest eye care centre in South China. Healthy individuals who accompanied their relatives with heart disease to the outpatient department of cardiovascular disease and systemically healthy patients who came for regular ophthalmic examination and had no relatives with heart disease were consecutively recruited for the study. A total of 1644 respondents with heart disease relatives and 813 respondents without heart disease relatives completed the survey. Thirty three per cent of respondents never heard of CPR and only 11% had received CPR training. Factors associated with a higher rate of CPR training were higher level of education and income (p<0.001). Most respondents stated that CPR training was necessary and would like to learn CPR. However, only one-third considered it beneficial to perform CPR as a layperson. In addition, healthcare respondents (p<0.001), younger (p<0.05) and more educated respondents (p<0.001) earned higher scores on the knowledge of CPR skills. Only 5.3% had perfect scores on a CPR skills test. Notably, respondents with relatives suffering from heart disease had significantly less training experience and CPR knowledge than those without (p<0.001). Although the attitudes towards learning CPR are very positive, there was a lack of knowledge on this topic among the general public. This study demonstrates an urgent need to boost awareness and training in CPR in South China, especially among people whose relatives have heart disease.
